Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 12, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

Tafsir of Surat Yusuf
[It is Makki] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]]

Al-Tha'labi and others narrated, through the chain of Salam ibn Sulaym (also said to be Sulaym) al-Mada'ini, who is abandoned (matruk), from Harun ibn Kathir (whose unknown status was explicitly stated by Abu Hatim), from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Teach your slaves Surat Yusuf, for whoever among Muslims recites it, or teaches it to his family, or to those his right hand possesses, Allah will make the agonies of death easy for him, and will give him the strength not to envy a Muslim." [[Tafsir al-Tha'labi (7/fol. 61, al-Mahmudiyya edition). Al-Zayla'i cited it in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/179) from al-Tha'labi's narration in his tafsir. Al-Wahidi narrated it in al-Wasit (2/599) through the chain of Ibrahim ibn Sharif from Ahmad ibn Yunus from Salam ibn Sulaym.]]

This narration, through this route, is not authentic, because its chain is entirely weak. Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir also related it as a supporting report (mutaba'ah) through the route of al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam, from Harun ibn Kathir, with the same wording; and through the route of Shababa, from Makhlad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Basri [[All manuscripts read: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Nadri"; manuscripts A and T read: "Makhlad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Nadri", and the correct form is what we have written.]], from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, and from 'Ata' ibn Abi Maymunah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar. [[Quoted by al-Zayla'i in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/180) from the author.]] It is munkar in all of its routes.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Dala'il that a group of Jews, when they heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting this surah, embraced Islam because it agreed with what they had. This is from the narration of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

As for the discussion of the disjointed letters, it has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

* *

His saying: ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾, meaning: these are the verses of the Book, which is the Qur'an, ﴿clear﴾, meaning: the plain and evident, which makes clear the ambiguous matters, explains them and makes them manifest.

﴿Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand﴾. That is because the language of the Arabs is the most eloquent of languages, the clearest, the most extensive, and the most capable of conveying the meanings that dwell in souls. Therefore the noblest Book was sent down in the noblest language, upon the noblest of Messengers, through the mediation of the noblest of angels, in the noblest place on earth, and its revelation began in the noblest month of the year, which is Ramadan. Thus it was perfect in every respect. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories, by Our revealing to you this Qur'an﴾, meaning, because of Our revealing this Qur'an to you.

It has been reported concerning the occasion of revelation of these verses what Ibn Jarir narrated:

Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me: Hakkam al-Razi narrated to us, from Ayyub, from 'Amr (who is Ibn Qays al-Mala'i), from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, would you relate to us?" So ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ was revealed. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/552).]]

He also narrated it through another route, from 'Amr ibn Qays, as a mursal report.

He also said: Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-'Attar [[In A: "Sa'd"; in T and A: "al-Qattan".]] narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Khallad al-Saffar informed us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from 'Amr ibn Murrah [[In T and A: "Qurrah".]], from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, who said: The Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ). He recited it to them for a time, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, would you relate to us?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book﴾ up to His saying: ﴿that you may understand﴾ [[In T: "(that you may understand) the verse".]]. Then he recited to them for a time, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, would you narrate to us?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾ [al-Zumar: 23], and he mentioned the hadith.

Al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi al-'Anqazi, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/553); al-Mustadrak (2/345), where he said: "A hadith with a sound chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar graded it hasan in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah, no. (3652).]]

Ibn Jarir also narrated with his chain, from al-Mas'udi, from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became weary of a particular weariness, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us something." [So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾.] Then they grew weary again and said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us more," [[Addition from T, A, and al-Tabari.]] above the hadith and below the Qur'an, by which they meant narratives. So Allah revealed: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand. We relate to you the best of stories by Our revealing to you this Qur'an, and indeed you were before it among the unaware.﴾ They wanted a hadith, so He guided them to the best of hadith, and they wanted narratives, so He guided them to the best of narratives. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/552).]]

Among what is fitting to mention at this noble verse, which includes praise of the Qur'an and that it suffices in place of every other book, is what Imam Ahmad said:

Suraij ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us, Hushaym informed us, Mujalid informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a book he had obtained from some of the People of the Book, and he read it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who became angry and said: "Are you bewildered by it, O son of al-Khattab? By the One in whose hand my soul is, I have brought it to you white and pure. Do not ask them about anything, for they will inform you of truth which you will deny, or of falsehood which you will affirm. By the One in whose hand my soul is, if Musa were alive, he would have no choice but to follow me." [[Al-Musnad (3/378).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Thabit, who said: 'Umar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I passed by a brother of mine from Qurayzah, and he wrote for me some comprehensive points from the Torah. Shall I present them to you?" He said: The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed. 'Abd Allah ibn Thabit said: I said to him: "Do you not see what is on the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" 'Umar said: "We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger." He said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) was relieved and said: "By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, even if Musa were to appear among you and you followed him and abandoned me, you would be led astray. You are my share among the nations, and I am your share among the Prophets." [[Al-Musnad (3/365).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Khalifah ibn Qays, from Khalid ibn 'Urfutah, who said: I was sitting with 'Umar when a man from 'Abd al-Qays, whose dwelling was in al-Sus, was brought to him. 'Umar said to him: "Are you so-and-so ibn so-and-so al-'Abdi?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And you are the one residing in al-Sus?" He said: "Yes." So he struck him with a staff he had with him. The man said: "What is my offence, O Commander of the Faithful?" 'Umar said to him: "Sit down." So he sat, and 'Umar recited to him: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand. We relate to you [the best of stories]﴾ [[Addition from T.]] up to His saying: ﴿indeed you were before it among the unaware﴾. He recited it three times and struck him three times. The man said: "What is my offence, O Commander of the Faithful?" 'Umar said: "You are the one who copied the book of Daniel!" He said: "Command me with your order and I will follow it." He said: "Go and wash it off with boiling water and white wool, then do not read it, nor have anyone among the people read it. If it reaches me that you have read it or taught it to anyone among the people, I will punish you with a severe punishment." Then he said to him: "Sit down," and he sat before him. He said: "I went and copied a book from the People of the Book, then I brought it to you on a piece of leather, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'What is this in your hand, O 'Umar?'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, it is a book I copied so that we might gain knowledge along with our knowledge." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry until his cheeks reddened. Then the call was made: "Assemble for prayer." The Ansar said: "Has your Prophet (ﷺ) become angry? Arms! Arms!" They came until they surrounded the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "O people, I have been given the comprehensive words and their conclusions, and it has been condensed for me in condensation. I have brought it to you white and pure, so do not be bewildered, and let not those who are bewildered deceive you." 'Umar said: I stood up and said: "I am content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with you as Messenger." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) descended. [[I did not find it in the printed Musnad of Abu Ya'la. It is cited by al-Haythami in al-Majma' (1/182), who said: "Abu Ya'la narrated it, and in its chain is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Wasiti, whom Ahmad and a group weakened." Al-Maqdisi narrated it in al-Mukhtarah, no. (115), through Abu Ya'la, and said: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, Muslim and Ibn Hibban narrated from him." He means 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Madani, who is more reliable than al-Wasiti, and their periods are close; but al-Mizzi mentioned 'Ali ibn Mushir among narrators from the weak al-Wasiti, and the author here favoured that it is al-Wasiti. Likewise in the Musnad of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (2/591), where it is said: "Al-Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi, in his book al-Mukhtarah, claimed that he is the one from whom Muslim narrated, as (I think the correct form is so) he said; and as for his teacher Khalifah ibn Qays, Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him: 'a shaykh not well known.' Al-Bukhari said: 'His hadith is not sound.'"]].

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his tafsir in abridged form, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, with the same. This is a gharib hadith from this route. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq is Abu Shaybah al-Wasiti, and they weakened him and his shaykh. Al-Bukhari said: "His hadith is not sound."

I said: A witness to this has also been transmitted by another route. The memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili said: Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed me; Ya'qub ibn Sufyan narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala' al-Zubaydi narrated to us; 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me; 'Abdullah ibn Salim al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from al-Zubaydi; Sulaym ibn 'Amir narrated to us: that Jubayr ibn Nufayr told them that two men were in Hims during the caliphate of 'Umar, may God be pleased with him. He sent for them, along with others he sent for from the people of Hims. They had copied some writings from the Jews, called ṣalāṣifa [in manuscript H: "mulāṣiq" without dots; the reading in T and A is adopted], and they took these with them, asking the Commander of the Believers about them, saying: "If the Commander of the Believers approves of them for us, we will be more eager for them, and if he forbids us from them, we will abandon them." When they came to him, they said: "We are in the land of the People of the Two Scriptures, and we hear from them words that make our skins shudder. Shall we take from it or leave it?" He said: "Perhaps you two have written something from it." They said: "No." He said: "I will tell you. I set out during the lifetime of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) until I came to Khaybar, and I found a Jew saying a saying that pleased me. I said: 'Will you dictate to me what you are saying?' He said: 'Yes.' So I brought a piece of leather, and he began dictating to me until I had written it on the al-akru' [the lower parts of the animal's legs]. When I returned, I said: 'O Prophet of God,' and I informed him. He said: 'Bring it to me.' So I set off, eager to avoid walking, hoping that I would bring the Messenger of God something of what he loves. When I brought it to him, he said: 'Sit down and read to me.' I read for a while, then I looked at his face, and it was changing color, so I was bewildered by the change. I could not even read a single letter from it. When he saw what was in me, he pushed it away, then began following it letter by letter, wiping it out with his saliva, and he was saying: 'Do not follow these people, for they have gone astray and have become confused,' until he had wiped out its last letter, letter by letter." 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: "If I had known that you two had written anything from it, I would have made you an example for this Ummah!" They said: "By God, we will never write anything from it again." So they left with their ṣalāṣifa, dug a hole for it, dug it deeply, buried it, and that was the last trace of it.

Similarly, al-Thawri narrated from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abdullah ibn Thabit al-Ansari, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, something similar. [Its takhrij has already been mentioned in the Musnad.] Abu Dawud also narrated in al-Marasil, from the hadith of Abu Qilabah, from 'Umar, something similar [al-Marasil, no. 455]. And God knows best.

The memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili said: Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed me; Ya'qub ibn Sufyan narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala' al-Zubaydi narrated to us; 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me; 'Abdullah ibn Salim al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from al-Zubaydi; Sulaym ibn 'Amir narrated to us: that Jubayr ibn Nufayr told them that two men were in Hims during the caliphate of 'Umar, may God be pleased with him. He sent for them, along with others he sent for from the people of Hims. They had copied some writings from the Jews, called ṣalāṣifa [in manuscript H: "mulāṣiq" without dots; the reading in T and A is adopted], and they took these with them, asking the Commander of the Believers about them, saying: "If the Commander of the Believers approves of them for us, we will be more eager for them, and if he forbids us from them, we will abandon them." When they came to him, they said: "We are in the land of the People of the Two Scriptures, and we hear from them words that make our skins shudder. Shall we take from it or leave it?" He said: "Perhaps you two have written something from it." They said: "No." He said: "I will tell you. I set out during the lifetime of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) until I came to Khaybar, and I found a Jew saying a saying that pleased me. I said: 'Will you dictate to me what you are saying?' He said: 'Yes.' So I brought a piece of leather, and he began dictating to me until I had written it on the al-akru' [the lower parts of the animal's legs]. When I returned, I said: 'O Prophet of God,' and I informed him. He said: 'Bring it to me.' So I set off, eager to avoid walking, hoping that I would bring the Messenger of God something of what he loves. When I brought it to him, he said: 'Sit down and read to me.' I read for a while, then I looked at his face, and it was changing color, so I was bewildered by the change. I could not even read a single letter from it. When he saw what was in me, he pushed it away, then began following it letter by letter, wiping it out with his saliva, and he was saying: 'Do not follow these people, for they have gone astray and have become confused,' until he had wiped out its last letter, letter by letter." 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: "If I had known that you two had written anything from it, I would have made you an example for this Ummah!" They said: "By God, we will never write anything from it again." So they left with their ṣalāṣifa, dug a hole for it, dug it deeply, buried it, and that was the last trace of it.

Similarly, al-Thawri narrated from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abdullah ibn Thabit al-Ansari, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, something similar. [Its takhrij has already been mentioned in the Musnad.] Abu Dawud also narrated in al-Marasil, from the hadith of Abu Qilabah, from 'Umar, something similar [al-Marasil, no. 455]. And God knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 12, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

Tafsir of Surat Yusuf
[It is Makki] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]]

Al-Tha'labi and others narrated, through the chain of Salam ibn Sulaym (also said to be Sulaym) al-Mada'ini, who is abandoned (matruk), from Harun ibn Kathir (whose unknown status was explicitly stated by Abu Hatim), from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Teach your slaves Surat Yusuf, for whoever among Muslims recites it, or teaches it to his family, or to those his right hand possesses, Allah will make the agonies of death easy for him, and will give him the strength not to envy a Muslim." [[Tafsir al-Tha'labi (7/fol. 61, al-Mahmudiyya edition). Al-Zayla'i cited it in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/179) from al-Tha'labi's narration in his tafsir. Al-Wahidi narrated it in al-Wasit (2/599) through the chain of Ibrahim ibn Sharif from Ahmad ibn Yunus from Salam ibn Sulaym.]]

This narration, through this route, is not authentic, because its chain is entirely weak. Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir also related it as a supporting report (mutaba'ah) through the route of al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam, from Harun ibn Kathir, with the same wording; and through the route of Shababa, from Makhlad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Basri [[All manuscripts read: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Nadri"; manuscripts A and T read: "Makhlad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Nadri", and the correct form is what we have written.]], from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, and from 'Ata' ibn Abi Maymunah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar. [[Quoted by al-Zayla'i in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/180) from the author.]] It is munkar in all of its routes.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Dala'il that a group of Jews, when they heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting this surah, embraced Islam because it agreed with what they had. This is from the narration of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

As for the discussion of the disjointed letters, it has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

* *

His saying: ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾, meaning: these are the verses of the Book, which is the Qur'an, ﴿clear﴾, meaning: the plain and evident, which makes clear the ambiguous matters, explains them and makes them manifest.

﴿Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand﴾. That is because the language of the Arabs is the most eloquent of languages, the clearest, the most extensive, and the most capable of conveying the meanings that dwell in souls. Therefore the noblest Book was sent down in the noblest language, upon the noblest of Messengers, through the mediation of the noblest of angels, in the noblest place on earth, and its revelation began in the noblest month of the year, which is Ramadan. Thus it was perfect in every respect. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories, by Our revealing to you this Qur'an﴾, meaning, because of Our revealing this Qur'an to you.

It has been reported concerning the occasion of revelation of these verses what Ibn Jarir narrated:

Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me: Hakkam al-Razi narrated to us, from Ayyub, from 'Amr (who is Ibn Qays al-Mala'i), from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, would you relate to us?" So ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ was revealed. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/552).]]

He also narrated it through another route, from 'Amr ibn Qays, as a mursal report.

He also said: Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-'Attar [[In A: "Sa'd"; in T and A: "al-Qattan".]] narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Khallad al-Saffar informed us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from 'Amr ibn Murrah [[In T and A: "Qurrah".]], from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, who said: The Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ). He recited it to them for a time, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, would you relate to us?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book﴾ up to His saying: ﴿that you may understand﴾ [[In T: "(that you may understand) the verse".]]. Then he recited to them for a time, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, would you narrate to us?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾ [al-Zumar: 23], and he mentioned the hadith.

Al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi al-'Anqazi, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/553); al-Mustadrak (2/345), where he said: "A hadith with a sound chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar graded it hasan in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah, no. (3652).]]

Ibn Jarir also narrated with his chain, from al-Mas'udi, from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became weary of a particular weariness, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us something." [So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾.] Then they grew weary again and said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us more," [[Addition from T, A, and al-Tabari.]] above the hadith and below the Qur'an, by which they meant narratives. So Allah revealed: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand. We relate to you the best of stories by Our revealing to you this Qur'an, and indeed you were before it among the unaware.﴾ They wanted a hadith, so He guided them to the best of hadith, and they wanted narratives, so He guided them to the best of narratives. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/552).]]

Among what is fitting to mention at this noble verse, which includes praise of the Qur'an and that it suffices in place of every other book, is what Imam Ahmad said:

Suraij ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us, Hushaym informed us, Mujalid informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a book he had obtained from some of the People of the Book, and he read it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who became angry and said: "Are you bewildered by it, O son of al-Khattab? By the One in whose hand my soul is, I have brought it to you white and pure. Do not ask them about anything, for they will inform you of truth which you will deny, or of falsehood which you will affirm. By the One in whose hand my soul is, if Musa were alive, he would have no choice but to follow me." [[Al-Musnad (3/378).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Thabit, who said: 'Umar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I passed by a brother of mine from Qurayzah, and he wrote for me some comprehensive points from the Torah. Shall I present them to you?" He said: The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed. 'Abd Allah ibn Thabit said: I said to him: "Do you not see what is on the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" 'Umar said: "We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger." He said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) was relieved and said: "By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, even if Musa were to appear among you and you followed him and abandoned me, you would be led astray. You are my share among the nations, and I am your share among the Prophets." [[Al-Musnad (3/365).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Khalifah ibn Qays, from Khalid ibn 'Urfutah, who said: I was sitting with 'Umar when a man from 'Abd al-Qays, whose dwelling was in al-Sus, was brought to him. 'Umar said to him: "Are you so-and-so ibn so-and-so al-'Abdi?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And you are the one residing in al-Sus?" He said: "Yes." So he struck him with a staff he had with him. The man said: "What is my offence, O Commander of the Faithful?" 'Umar said to him: "Sit down." So he sat, and 'Umar recited to him: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand. We relate to you [the best of stories]﴾ [[Addition from T.]] up to His saying: ﴿indeed you were before it among the unaware﴾. He recited it three times and struck him three times. The man said: "What is my offence, O Commander of the Faithful?" 'Umar said: "You are the one who copied the book of Daniel!" He said: "Command me with your order and I will follow it." He said: "Go and wash it off with boiling water and white wool, then do not read it, nor have anyone among the people read it. If it reaches me that you have read it or taught it to anyone among the people, I will punish you with a severe punishment." Then he said to him: "Sit down," and he sat before him. He said: "I went and copied a book from the People of the Book, then I brought it to you on a piece of leather, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'What is this in your hand, O 'Umar?'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, it is a book I copied so that we might gain knowledge along with our knowledge." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry until his cheeks reddened. Then the call was made: "Assemble for prayer." The Ansar said: "Has your Prophet (ﷺ) become angry? Arms! Arms!" They came until they surrounded the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "O people, I have been given the comprehensive words and their conclusions, and it has been condensed for me in condensation. I have brought it to you white and pure, so do not be bewildered, and let not those who are bewildered deceive you." 'Umar said: I stood up and said: "I am content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with you as Messenger." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) descended. [[I did not find it in the printed Musnad of Abu Ya'la. It is cited by al-Haythami in al-Majma' (1/182), who said: "Abu Ya'la narrated it, and in its chain is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Wasiti, whom Ahmad and a group weakened." Al-Maqdisi narrated it in al-Mukhtarah, no. (115), through Abu Ya'la, and said: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, Muslim and Ibn Hibban narrated from him." He means 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Madani, who is more reliable than al-Wasiti, and their periods are close; but al-Mizzi mentioned 'Ali ibn Mushir among narrators from the weak al-Wasiti, and the author here favoured that it is al-Wasiti. Likewise in the Musnad of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (2/591), where it is said: "Al-Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi, in his book al-Mukhtarah, claimed that he is the one from whom Muslim narrated, as (I think the correct form is so) he said; and as for his teacher Khalifah ibn Qays, Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him: 'a shaykh not well known.' Al-Bukhari said: 'His hadith is not sound.'"]].

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his tafsir in abridged form, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, with the same. This is a gharib hadith from this route. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq is Abu Shaybah al-Wasiti, and they weakened him and his shaykh. Al-Bukhari said: "His hadith is not sound."

I said: A witness to this has also been transmitted by another route. The memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili said: Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed me; Ya'qub ibn Sufyan narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala' al-Zubaydi narrated to us; 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me; 'Abdullah ibn Salim al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from al-Zubaydi; Sulaym ibn 'Amir narrated to us: that Jubayr ibn Nufayr told them that two men were in Hims during the caliphate of 'Umar, may God be pleased with him. He sent for them, along with others he sent for from the people of Hims. They had copied some writings from the Jews, called ṣalāṣifa [in manuscript H: "mulāṣiq" without dots; the reading in T and A is adopted], and they took these with them, asking the Commander of the Believers about them, saying: "If the Commander of the Believers approves of them for us, we will be more eager for them, and if he forbids us from them, we will abandon them." When they came to him, they said: "We are in the land of the People of the Two Scriptures, and we hear from them words that make our skins shudder. Shall we take from it or leave it?" He said: "Perhaps you two have written something from it." They said: "No." He said: "I will tell you. I set out during the lifetime of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) until I came to Khaybar, and I found a Jew saying a saying that pleased me. I said: 'Will you dictate to me what you are saying?' He said: 'Yes.' So I brought a piece of leather, and he began dictating to me until I had written it on the al-akru' [the lower parts of the animal's legs]. When I returned, I said: 'O Prophet of God,' and I informed him. He said: 'Bring it to me.' So I set off, eager to avoid walking, hoping that I would bring the Messenger of God something of what he loves. When I brought it to him, he said: 'Sit down and read to me.' I read for a while, then I looked at his face, and it was changing color, so I was bewildered by the change. I could not even read a single letter from it. When he saw what was in me, he pushed it away, then began following it letter by letter, wiping it out with his saliva, and he was saying: 'Do not follow these people, for they have gone astray and have become confused,' until he had wiped out its last letter, letter by letter." 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: "If I had known that you two had written anything from it, I would have made you an example for this Ummah!" They said: "By God, we will never write anything from it again." So they left with their ṣalāṣifa, dug a hole for it, dug it deeply, buried it, and that was the last trace of it.

Similarly, al-Thawri narrated from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abdullah ibn Thabit al-Ansari, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, something similar. [Its takhrij has already been mentioned in the Musnad.] Abu Dawud also narrated in al-Marasil, from the hadith of Abu Qilabah, from 'Umar, something similar [al-Marasil, no. 455]. And God knows best.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, the Exalted, says: Mention to your people, O Muhammad, in your narration to them, the story of Yusuf (Joseph), when he said to his father, and his father was Ya'qub (Jacob), peace be upon him, as Imam Ahmad said:

Narrated to us 'Abd al-Samad: narrated to us 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from his father, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The generous, son of the generous, son of the generous, son of the generous: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim."

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it. He related it from 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Samad with this chain. [[Musnad (2/96) and Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4688).]] Al-Bukhari also said:

Narrated to us Muhammad: 'Abdah informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Who is the most noble of people?" He said: "The most noble of them in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of them." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then the most noble of people is Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the friend of Allah." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then are you asking me about the mines of the Arabs?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then the best of you in the Jahiliyyah are the best of you in Islam, when they gain understanding." Then he said: Abu Usamah followed him, from 'Ubayd Allah. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4689).]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: The visions of the prophets are revelation.

The commentators have discussed the interpretation of this dream: that the eleven stars represent his brothers, who were eleven men [besides him], and the sun and the moon represent his father and mother. This was related from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Sufyan al-Thawri, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. Its interpretation came to pass after forty years, and it was said eighty years, when he raised his parents upon the throne, and it is his seat, and his brothers were before him: "And they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, 'O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true.'" [Yusuf: 100]

Concerning the naming of these eleven stars, there has come a narration, and Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said:

Narrated to me 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi: narrated to us al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr, from al-Suddi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, [from Jabir], who said: A man of the Jews, called "Bustanah al-Yahudi", came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: "O Muhammad, tell me about the stars which Yusuf saw prostrating to him, what are their names?" He said: The Prophet ﷺ was silent for a while and did not answer him with anything, and Jibril, peace be upon him, descended and informed him of their names. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for him and said: "Will you believe if I inform you of their names?" He said: Yes. He said: "Kharatan, al-Tariq, al-Dhayyal, Dhu al-Kanafat, Qabis, Waththab, 'Amudan, al-Faylaq, al-Musabbih, al-Darrah, Dhu al-Far', al-Diya', and al-Nur." The Jew said: "By Allah, indeed these are their names." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/555).]]

It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in "al-Dala'il", from the narration of Sa'id ibn Mansur, from al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr. This hadith was also narrated by the two memorizers Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili and Abu Bakr al-Bazzar in their Musnads, and Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir. [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (6/277), Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2220), "Kashf al-Astar". There is difference in the names of the stars in these sources, which is not significant; Ibn al-Jawzi judged the hadith to be fabricated.]] As for Abu Ya'la, he narrated it from four of his teachers, from al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr, with it, and added: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Yusuf saw them, he related them to his father Ya'qub, and his father said to him: 'This is a scattered matter which Allah will later gather together.' He said: 'And the sun is his father, and the moon is his mother.'"

al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr al-Fazari alone narrated it. [[It was not narrated by him alone; it was followed up. al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (4/396) through Talhah from Asbat ibn Nasr, from al-Suddi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Jabir, similar to it, and he said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the conditions of Muslim, though they did not record it." al-Zayla'i said: "The chain of al-Hakim comes against al-Bazzar in his saying: we do not know a path for it other than this, and against al-Bayhaqi in his saying: al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr alone narrated it, and they both have their excuse." Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/161).]] The imams have weakened him, most of them abandoned him, and al-Jawzajani said: "Discarded, and he is the narrator of the hadith 'the beauty of Yusuf'."

Allah says, reporting the words of Ya'qub (Jacob) to his son Yusuf (Joseph) when he related to him what he had seen in this dream, whose interpretation is the submission of his brothers to him and their exceeding honor of him, to the extent that they would fall down prostrating before him out of reverence, honor and respect [[In manuscripts T and A: "واحتراما وإكراما" (wa-ihtiraman wa-ikraman).]]. So Ya'qub, peace be upon him, feared that he might tell any of his brothers about this dream, and they would envy him for it and plot harm against him out of jealousy. For this reason he said to him: ﴿Do not relate your dream to your brothers, lest they devise a scheme against you﴾, meaning: they will contrive a plot against you by which they will bring you to ruin.

For this reason the Sunnah has been established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "If one of you sees something he loves, let him relate it, but if he sees something he dislikes, let him turn onto his other side, spit three times to his left, seek refuge in Allah from its evil, and not relate it to anyone, for it will not harm him." [[This comes from the hadith of Jabir, Umm Salamah and Abu Qatadah. As for the hadith of Jabir, it is narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2262). As for the hadith of Umm Salamah, it is narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (10741). As for the hadith of Abu Qatadah, it is narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (5/296), and this is its wording.]]

And in another hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and some of the authors of the Sunan, through the narration of Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A dream is on the foot of a bird as long as it is not interpreted; once it is interpreted, it comes to pass." [[I have not located it from the hadith of Mu'awiyah, but rather from the hadith of Laqit ibn Amir, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/10), Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. (5020), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (2278), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan no. (3914).]]

From this is derived the instruction to conceal a blessing until it is obtained and becomes apparent, as occurs in the hadith: "Seek help in fulfilling your needs by keeping them secret, for every person who has a blessing is envied." [[Narrated by al-'Uqayli in al-Du'afa' (2/109), Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (3/404), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (6/96), through the route of Sa'id ibn Salim al-'Attar from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Mu'adh, with it as a marfu' report. Ibn al-Jawzi included it in al-Mawdu'at (2/165), and Abu Hatim said in al-'Ilal (2/258): "A munkar hadith." Its defect is Sa'id ibn Salam al-'Attar, who is a liar.]]

Ibn Kathir said, reporting the words of Ya'qub (Jacob) to his son Yusuf (Joseph): "Just as your Lord has chosen you, and has shown you these stars along with the sun and the moon prostrating to you, ﴿And thus your Lord will choose you﴾, that is, He will select you and choose you for His prophethood, ﴿and will teach you the interpretation of events (ta'wil al-ahadith)﴾." Mujahid and others said: this means the interpretation of dreams (ta'bir al-ru'ya).

﴿And will complete His favour upon you﴾, that is, by sending you as a messenger and revealing to you. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means he will run about and be active. Likewise said Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and others.

Allah, the Exalted, says, reporting about His Prophet Ya'qub [[In T and A: "about the Prophet of Allah"]], that he said to his sons, in reply to their request that they send Yusuf with them to pasture the flocks in the desert: ﴿Indeed, it grieves me that you take him away﴾, meaning: it is hard for me to be parted from him for the whole time you are gone with him until he returns. This was due to his intense love for him, because of the great good he perceived in him and the marks of prophethood and perfection in his character and form, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And I fear that a wolf will eat him while you are heedless of him﴾ means: I fear that you will busy yourselves away from him with your shooting and your herding, so a wolf will come to him and eat him while you are unaware. They took this statement from his mouth and made it their excuse for what they had done, and they answered it right then, saying: ﴿If the wolf eats him while we are a band, then indeed we would be losers﴾. They are saying: if the wolf attacks him and eats him from among us while we are a group, then indeed we would be doomed and powerless.

Allah the Exalted says: "So when they took him away and agreed to put him into the depths of the well" (Qur'an 12:15). Here there is an emphasis on what they did: that they all agreed to throw him to the bottom of that well, although they had taken him from his father's presence, showing him honour, gladdening his heart and making him happy. It is said that when Ya'qub (peace be upon him) sent him with them, he embraced him, kissed him and prayed for him.

As-Suddi and others said: There was no gap between their showing him honour and displaying harm towards him, except that they went out of their father's sight and hid from him. Then they began to harm him with words, such as insults and the like, and with deeds, such as beating and the like. Then they brought him to that well into which they had agreed to throw him, tied him with a rope and lowered him into it. Whenever he sought refuge with one of them, he would slap him and insult him, and whenever he clung to the edges of the well, they struck his hands. Then they cut the rope for him halfway down, so he fell into the water and it covered him. He climbed onto a rock in the middle of it, called "ar-Raghufah" (the rock), and stood upon it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We inspired him: "You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they do not perceive."﴾ Allah the Exalted, mentioning His gentleness, mercy, kindness and His bringing of ease in a time of hardship, says: He inspired Yusuf in that narrow situation, to comfort his heart and to strengthen him: "Do not grieve over what you are in, for you will have from it relief and a good outcome, Allah will help you against them, exalt you, raise your rank, and you will inform them of what they did to you by this deed."

* *

As for His saying ﴿while they do not perceive﴾: Mujahid and Qatadah said: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ refers to the inspiration of Allah to him.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "You will inform them of this deed of theirs against you, while they do not recognise you and do not sense that it is you." As Ibn Jarir said:

Al-Harith narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn 'Ubadah al-Asadi narrated to us, from his father, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: When the brothers of Yusuf entered upon Yusuf, he recognised them while they did not recognise him. He said: The drinking cup was brought, and he placed it on his hand, then struck it so that it hummed, and said: "This cup tells me that you had a brother from your father called 'Yusuf', whom your father favoured over you, and that you took him away and threw him into the depths of the well." He said: Then he struck it again so that it hummed, "and you came to your father and said: 'A wolf ate him,' and you brought his shirt stained with false blood." He said: Then some of them said to others: "This cup is telling him about our affair." Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: We do not think this verse was revealed except concerning them: ﴿You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they do not perceive.﴾

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the plan that Yusuf's brothers adopted after they had thrown him into the depths of the well: that they returned to their father in the darkness of the night, weeping, showing grief and distress over Yusuf, and pretending to their father [that they were sorry]. They said, making excuses for what had happened, according to what they claimed: ﴿Indeed, we went off racing one another﴾, i.e., competing in running, ﴿and we left Yusuf by our belongings﴾, i.e., our clothes and goods, ﴿and the wolf devoured him﴾, and it was the very thing he had feared and been anxious about for him.

* *

As for their saying: ﴿And you would not believe us even if we were truthful﴾, it is a great softening of speech in establishing what they were attempting, as if they were saying: "We know that you would not believe us in this state even if we were truthful in your sight. How then, when you accuse us of this, since you feared that the wolf would devour him, and then the wolf did devour him? You are excused in disbelieving us, because of the strangeness of what occurred and the wondrous thing that befell us in this matter of ours."

﴿And they brought his shirt with false blood﴾, i.e., fabricated and invented. This is among the actions by which they sought to confirm the deception on which they had colluded. They had gone to a young goat, as reported by Mujahid, al-Suddi and others, slaughtered it, and smeared Yusuf's garment with its blood, giving the impression that this was the shirt in which the wolf had devoured him and that it had been stained with his blood. But they forgot to tear it. Therefore this deed did not deceive the Prophet of Allah Ya'qub; rather, he said to them, turning away from their words toward what was in his own heart about their collusion against him: ﴿Rather, your souls have made a matter attractive to you, so patience is fitting [sabrun jamil]﴾, i.e., I shall be patient with a good patience regarding this matter upon which you have agreed, until Allah relieves it by His help and kindness. ﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾, i.e., against what you mention of lies and impossibilities.

Al-Thawri reported from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding: ﴿And they brought his shirt with false blood﴾, that he said: "If a beast of prey had devoured him, it would have torn the shirt." Similarly said al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others.

Mujahid said: "Patient beauty (al-sabr al-jamil) is that in which there is no complaint (jaza')."

Hushaym narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya, from Habban ibn Abi Jabalah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about His saying: ﴿so patience is fitting﴾, and he said: "Patience in which there is no complaint." This is a mursal report.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri said, from some of his companions, that he said: "There are three forms of patience: that you do not speak of your pain, nor of your calamity, and that you do not praise yourself."

Al-Bukhari mentioned here the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning the slander (al-ifk), up to where she said: "By Allah, I cannot find for myself and for you an example except the father of Yusuf," ﴿so patience is fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri said, from some of his companions, that he said: "There are three forms of patience: that you do not speak of your pain, nor of your calamity, and that you do not praise yourself."

Al-Bukhari mentioned here the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning the slander (al-ifk), up to where she said: "By Allah, I cannot find for myself and for you an example except the father of Yusuf," ﴿so patience is fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾.

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the plan that Yusuf's brothers adopted after they had thrown him into the depths of the well: that they returned to their father in the darkness of the night, weeping, showing grief and distress over Yusuf, and pretending to their father [that they were sorry]. They said, making excuses for what had happened, according to what they claimed: ﴿Indeed, we went off racing one another﴾, i.e., competing in running, ﴿and we left Yusuf by our belongings﴾, i.e., our clothes and goods, ﴿and the wolf devoured him﴾, and it was the very thing he had feared and been anxious about for him.

* *

As for their saying: ﴿And you would not believe us even if we were truthful﴾, it is a great softening of speech in establishing what they were attempting, as if they were saying: "We know that you would not believe us in this state even if we were truthful in your sight. How then, when you accuse us of this, since you feared that the wolf would devour him, and then the wolf did devour him? You are excused in disbelieving us, because of the strangeness of what occurred and the wondrous thing that befell us in this matter of ours."

﴿And they brought his shirt with false blood﴾, i.e., fabricated and invented. This is among the actions by which they sought to confirm the deception on which they had colluded. They had gone to a young goat, as reported by Mujahid, al-Suddi and others, slaughtered it, and smeared Yusuf's garment with its blood, giving the impression that this was the shirt in which the wolf had devoured him and that it had been stained with his blood. But they forgot to tear it. Therefore this deed did not deceive the Prophet of Allah Ya'qub; rather, he said to them, turning away from their words toward what was in his own heart about their collusion against him: ﴿Rather, your souls have made a matter attractive to you, so patience is fitting [sabrun jamil]﴾, i.e., I shall be patient with a good patience regarding this matter upon which you have agreed, until Allah relieves it by His help and kindness. ﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾, i.e., against what you mention of lies and impossibilities.

Al-Thawri reported from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding: ﴿And they brought his shirt with false blood﴾, that he said: "If a beast of prey had devoured him, it would have torn the shirt." Similarly said al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others.

Mujahid said: "Patient beauty (al-sabr al-jamil) is that in which there is no complaint (jaza')."

Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah Yusuf (12), verses 19–20:

God, exalted is He, says, informing of what happened to Yusuf (peace be upon him) when his brothers cast him down and left him alone and solitary in that well. He remained in the well for three days, according to what Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash said [[In manuscript T, "Ibn 'Abbas".]].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When his brothers cast him down, they sat around the well that day, watching what he would do and what would be done to him. God caused a caravan (sayyarah) to come to them, and they stopped near that well. They sent their water-seeker (warid), who is the one who seeks water for them. When he came to that well and lowered his bucket into it, Yusuf (peace be upon him) grasped it. He pulled him out and rejoiced at him, and said: ﴿O what good news! This is a boy!﴾

Some reciters read: "Ya bushra" (O good news). Al-Suddi claimed that it is the name of a man, whom that man who lowered his bucket called, informing him that he had found a boy. This statement of al-Suddi is strange, because the interpretation of this reading in this way has not been preceded except in a narration from Ibn 'Abbas, and God knows best. The meaning of the reading in this manner returns to the other reading. He attributed the good news (bushra) to himself and dropped the possessive yā' while intending it, as the Arabs say: "Yā nafsu isbirī" (O self, be patient), and "Yā ghulāmu aqbil" (O boy, come here), by dropping the letter of attachment. The kasra and the raf' are permissible in that case. This is one of them, and the other reading ﴿O good news!﴾ clarifies it, and God knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾ means: the water-seekers from the rest of the caravan concealed him and said: "We bought him and took him as merchandise from the owners of the water," fearing that they would share in him if they learned of his situation. This was said by Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir. This is one opinion.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And they concealed him as merchandise﴾: it means the brothers of Yusuf concealed his affair and hid that he was their brother. Yusuf also concealed his affair, fearing that his brothers would kill him, and he chose to be sold. So his brothers mentioned him to the caravan's water-seeker, and he called out to his companions: ﴿O good news! This is a boy!﴾ for sale, and his brothers sold him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And God is Knowing of what they do﴾ means: He knows what the brothers of Yusuf and his buyers do. He is capable of changing that and repelling it, but He has wisdom and a predetermined decree, so He left that to carry out what He had decreed and decided. Indeed, to Him belong the creation and the command. Blessed is God, Lord of the worlds.

In this there is an indirect address to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) [[In manuscript T: "Peace and blessings of God be upon him"; in manuscript A: "Peace and blessings of God be upon him and grant him peace".]], and an informing to him that I know the harm of your people, and I am able to deny it to them, but I will give them respite, then I will make the final outcome and the judgment for you over them, just as I made the judgment and the final outcome for Yusuf over his brothers.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, a few dirhams counted﴾ says God, exalted is He: his brothers sold him for a small price. This was said by Mujahid and 'Ikrimah.

Al-bakhs means deficiency, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So he fears no injustice or burden﴾ [al-Jinn: 13], meaning: his brothers exchanged him for a price that was low and small. Yet they were, despite that, among those who had no desire for him; that is, they had no inclination towards him, and if he had been asked for free, they would have agreed.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak said: the pronoun in His saying ﴿And they sold him﴾ refers to the brothers of Yusuf.

Qatadah said: rather, it refers to the caravan.

The first is stronger, because His saying ﴿and they were among those who had no desire for him﴾ intends only his brothers, not those caravan people, since the caravan rejoiced at him and concealed him as merchandise. Had they been disinclined towards him, they would not have bought him. Therefore it is preferred that the pronoun in ﴿And they sold him﴾ refers to his brothers.

It was said: the intended meaning of His saying ﴿bakhs﴾ is the unlawful (ḥarām). It was also said: injustice (ẓulm). Although this may be so, it is not the intended meaning here, because it is well known and everyone knows that his price was unlawful in every case and for everyone, since he is a prophet, son of a prophet, son of a prophet, son of the Friend of the Merciful (Ibrahim), so he is noble, son of a noble, son of a noble, son of a noble. Rather, the intended meaning of bakhs here is deficient, or counterfeit, or both: that is, they were his brothers, and they sold him, and that for the lowest of prices. For this reason He said: ﴿a few dirhams counted﴾. From Ibn Mas'ud: they sold him for twenty dirhams. Ibn 'Abbas, Nawf al-Bakali, al-Suddi, Qatadah, and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi also said this, and added: they divided it between them, two dirhams each.

Mujahid said: twenty-two dirhams.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq and 'Ikrimah said: forty dirhams.

Al-Dahhak said, regarding His saying ﴿and they were among those who had no desire for him﴾: that is because they did not know of his prophethood and his high station with God, the Mighty and Majestic.

Mujahid said: when they sold him, they began to follow them, saying to them: "Secure him, so that he does not run away," until they stopped with him in Egypt. He said: "Who will buy me and be glad (of it)?" So the king bought him, and he was a Muslim.

[﴿She, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him﴾] from himself, meaning she tried to seduce him and invited him to herself. [[Addition from T, A.]] [[In T, A: "from".]] This was because she loved him intensely for his beauty, his comeliness and his splendour. The reciters differed over the reading of ﴿hayta laka﴾. Many read it with a fatha on the ha', a sukun on the ya', and a fatha on the ta'. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said its meaning is that she was inviting him to herself. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas that ﴿hayta laka﴾ means "come, for you." Likewise said Zirr ibn Hubaysh, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan and Qatadah.

'Amr ibn 'Ubayd related from al-Hasan: it is a word in Syriac, meaning "upon you" [or "come"].

al-Suddi said: ﴿hayta laka﴾ means "come, for you," and it is in Coptic.

Mujahid said: it is an Arabic dialect word by which she summoned him.

al-Bukhari said: 'Ikrimah said: ﴿hayta laka﴾ means "come, for you," in the Hawrani dialect.

He mentioned it in this way without a chain, but Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) traced it with a full chain: Ahmad ibn Suhayl al-Wasiti narrated to me, Qurrah ibn Qays narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi al-Jazari [[In T: "+Gharbi +al-Hawri".]] narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, the freedman of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿hayta laka﴾: he said, "come, for you." He said, "It is in the Hawrani dialect."

Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam said: al-Kisa'i used to relate this reading, meaning ﴿hayta laka﴾, and say: "It is a dialect of the people of Hawran that reached the people of the Hijaz, and its meaning is 'come.'" Abu 'Ubayd said: I asked a learned elder from the people of Hawran, and he mentioned that it is their dialect, which they recognise.

Imam Ibn Jarir cited in support of this reading the verse of a poet addressed to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him:

"Convey to the Commander of the Faithful, brother of Iraq, when we come [to him]...
Indeed Iraq and its people are a neck turned toward you, so hayta hayta."

He says: meaning, "come near."

Others read it as "hi'tu laka" with a kasra on the ha' and the hamza, and a damma on the ta', meaning "I have prepared myself for you," from the saying of one who says "hi'tu li-l-amr, ahayu hay'ah" (I readied myself for the matter). Among those related from as reading thus were Ibn 'Abbas, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Wa'il, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah, and all of them explained it as "I have prepared myself for you."

Ibn Jarir said: Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i used to reject this reading. 'Abd Allah ibn Ishaq read "hayti" with a fatha on the ha' and a kasra on the ta', and it is a rare reading.

Others, among them the majority of the people of Madinah, read "hayta" with a fatha on the ha' and a damma on the ta', and they cited the verse of the poet:

"My people are not the most distant when a summoner from the clan says: 'hayta!'"

'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "I have heard the reciters, and I heard them as near to one another. So recite as you were taught, and beware of excessive rigidity and disagreement, for it is only like the saying of one of you, 'halumma' and 'ta'al' (both meaning come)." Then 'Abd Allah recited ﴿hayta laka﴾. A man said to him: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, some people recite it as 'hayta laka'?" 'Abd Allah said: "I recite it as I was taught, which is more beloved to me."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn WakI' narrated to me, Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, who said: 'Abd Allah said: ﴿hayta laka﴾. Masruq said to him: "Some people recite it as 'hayta laka'?" He said: "Leave me, for I recite as I was taught, which is more beloved to me."

He also said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: ﴿hayta laka﴾ with a fatha on the ha' and the ta', and without a hamza.

Others said: "Hiyta laka," with a kasra on the ha', a sukun on the ya', and a damma on the ta'.

Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna said: "Hayta" is not dualised, nor pluralised, nor feminised; rather, all are addressed with one form, so one says: hayta laka, hayta laka, hayta lakuma, hayta lakum, hayta lahunna. [[In A: "lahum".]]

The disagreement of the scholars and their expressions on this matter is extensive. It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and a group of the early scholars (al-salaf) what Ibn Jarir and others have mentioned, and Allah knows best.

Some of them said: What is meant by his intention (hamm) to her is the intention of the passing thoughts of the soul (khatarat hadith al-nafs). Al-Baghawi related this from some of the people of verification (ahl al-tahqiq). Then al-Baghawi cited here the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah the Exalted says: When My servant intends a good deed, write it for him as a good deed. If he does it, write it for him as ten times its like. If he intends an evil deed and does not do it, write it for him as a good deed, for he has left it only for My sake. If he does it, write it as its like."

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs, and it has many wordings, of which this is one.

It has also been said: He intended to strike her. It has been said: He desired her as a wife. It has been said: The verse ﴿And he intended her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾ means: he did not intend her.

There is an objection to this view from the standpoint of the Arabic language, as Ibn Jarir and others have mentioned. [Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (16/38, 39). What the Hafiz mentions here regarding the meaning of hamm is not accepted without reservation. The preferred view is that chosen by Abu Hayyan in his tafsir, which al-'Allamah al-Shinqiti transmitted from him in "Adwa' al-Bayan" (3/60), where he said: "The second answer, which is the one Abu Hayyan chose, is that Yusuf did not have any intention at all; rather, it is negated from him because of the presence of the proof..." And see the rest of his statement there.]

As for the proof (burhan) that he saw, there are also several views. From Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Salih, al-Dahhak, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others: he saw the image of his father Ya'qub, peace be upon him, biting on his finger with his mouth.

It has also been related from him in one narration: he struck Yusuf in the chest.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: he saw the phantom (khayal) of the king, meaning his master. Likewise Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, relating from some of them: it was only the phantom of Itfir, his master, when he approached the door. [Footnote: Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said in al-Fatawa (10/297): "As for what is transmitted, that he loosened his trousers, sat in the position of a man with a woman, and that he saw the image of Ya'qub biting his hand, and similar things, these are matters Allah and His Messenger did not inform us of. What is not like that is taken from the Jews, who are among the greatest of people in lying about the prophets and disparaging them, and every Muslim who transmitted it, transmitted it from them. Not one of these things was transmitted from our Prophet ﷺ even a single letter." See also: Al-Isra'iliyyat fi Kutub al-Tafsir (the Israelite narratives in tafsir books) by Muhammad Abu Shahbah (pp. 220-225).]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Mawdud (in T: "Mardud"), I heard from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: Yusuf raised his head to the ceiling of the house, and there was a writing on the wall of the house: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way﴾ [Al-Isra: 32].

Abu Ma'shar al-Madani also related it similarly from Muhammad ibn Ka'b.

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from Abu Sakhr, who said: I heard al-Qurazi say concerning the "proof" that Yusuf saw: three verses from the Book of Allah: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-Infitar: 10], and His saying: ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair﴾ up to the end of the verse [Yunus: 61], and His saying: ﴿Then is He who is standing over every soul in what it has earned...﴾ [Al-Ra'd: 33]. Nafi' said: I heard Abu Hilal say the same as the saying of al-Qurazi, and he added a fourth verse: ﴿And do not approach adultery﴾ [Al-Isra: 32].

Al-Awza'i said: He saw a verse from the Book of Allah on the wall forbidding him from that.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct position is to say that he saw one of the signs of Allah which restrained him from what he had intended. It is permissible that it was the image of Ya'qub, and it is permissible that it was the image of the king, and it is permissible that what he saw was written prohibition against that. There is no conclusive proof specifying any one of these, so the correct approach is to leave it general as Allah the Exalted has said.

He said: And His saying: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil and immorality﴾ means: just as We showed him a proof that turned him away from what he was engaged in, so We protect him from evil and immorality in all his affairs.

﴿Indeed, he was among Our chosen servants﴾ means: among those who are selected, purified, chosen, elected, and the best, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Ibn Kathir said, on the words of Allah, the Exalted, about their condition when they both raced toward the door. Yusuf was fleeing while the woman was pursuing him to bring him back into the house. She caught up with him in the course of that, and she seized his shirt [from behind] [[addition from manuscripts T and A.]] and tore it badly. It is said that it was torn from him, and Yusuf continued fleeing and going, with her following in his trail. Then they found her master, who was her husband, at the door. At that point she got herself out of her predicament by her deceit and her scheming. She said to her husband, disclaiming responsibility and accusing Yusuf with her own lie: ﴿What is the punishment for one who intended evil for your wife?﴾ That is, [in T and A: "meaning"] adultery. ﴿Except that he be imprisoned﴾ that is, be confined, ﴿or a painful punishment﴾ that is, be beaten severely and painfully. At that point Yusuf, peace be upon him, defended himself with the truth, cleared himself of what she had charged him with of betrayal, and said, speaking righteously and truthfully: ﴿It was she who sought to seduce me﴾. It is mentioned that she followed him, pulling him toward herself, until she tore his shirt. ﴿And a witness from her family testified: If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is a liar﴾ that is, from in front of him, ﴿then she has told the truth﴾ that is, in her claim that he wanted to force himself upon her, because when he invited her and she refused, he pushed her away in her chest, and so she tore his shirt, and what she said is then sound. ﴿But if his shirt is torn from behind, then she has lied and he is of the truthful﴾. That would be consistent with what happened when he fled from her and she pursued him, seizing his shirt from behind to pull him back to her, and so tearing his shirt from behind.

Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Suddi said: he was her paternal cousin.

Ibn ʿAbbas also said: he was one of the king's close associates.

Ibn Ishaq mentioned that Zulaykha was the daughter of the king's sister, al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid.

It is said that it was torn from him, and Yusuf continued fleeing and going, with her following in his trail. Then they found her master, who was her husband, at the door. At that point she got herself out of her predicament by her deceit and her scheming. We were told by Israʾil, from Simak, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾ He said: "A man with a beard."

Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Suddi said: he was her paternal cousin.

Ibn ʿAbbas also said: he was one of the king's close associates.

Ibn Ishaq mentioned that Zulaykha was the daughter of the king's sister, al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah Yusuf (12), verses 30–34:

God, exalted is He, informs us that the news of Yusuf and the wife of the Governor (al-'Aziz) spread throughout the city, which was Egypt, until people talked about it. ﴿And women in the city said﴾ (like the wives of the great leaders and nobles [and] [[addition from T, A.]]) disapproving of the wife of the Governor, who was the minister, and condemning this of her: ﴿The wife of the Governor is seeking to seduce her young man from himself﴾, i.e., she is trying to get her slave to yield himself to her, and inviting him to herself. ﴿She has been overcome by love for him﴾, i.e., his love has reached the innermost part of her heart. Shaghaf is its covering.

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Shaghaf is love that kills, and shaghaf is less than that. Al-shaghaf is the veil of the heart."

﴿Indeed, we see her in clear error﴾, i.e., in this act of hers, of loving her young man and seeking to seduce him into herself.

﴿When she heard of their scheming﴾. Some said: "Of their words." Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "Rather, the news of Yusuf's beauty reached them, so they wished to see him, and they said that in order to find a way to see him and look at him. At that point, ﴿she sent for them﴾, i.e., she invited them to her house to entertain them, ﴿and prepared for them a mutaka'﴾."

Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Suddi and others said: it is the prepared gathering, in which there are cushions, pillows and food, including things that are cut with knives, such as citron and the like. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and she gave each one of them a knife﴾. This was a stratagem on her part and a counter to their own scheming to see him. ﴿And she said: "Come out before them"﴾, for she had hidden him in another place. ﴿When﴾ he came out and ﴿they saw him, they magnified him﴾, i.e., they greatly exalted his status and esteemed his rank, and they began to cut their hands in bewilderment at seeing him, thinking they were cutting the citron with the knives. The meaning is that they gashed their hands with them, as stated by more than one scholar.

It is also reported from Mujahid and Qatadah: they cut their hands until they threw them away. And God knows best.

It has been mentioned from Zayd ibn Aslam that she said to them, after they had eaten and their souls were content, and after she had placed citron before them and given each one of them a knife: "Would you like to look at Yusuf?" They said, "Yes." So she sent to him, ordering him to come out to them. When they saw him they began to cut their hands. Then she ordered him to return, and he returned so that they could see him coming and going, while they kept gashing their hands. When they felt the pain they began to wail. She said: "From one glance you have done this! How then can I be blamed?" They said: "Far be God from it! This is not a human; this is nothing but a noble angel." Then they said to her: "We do not see any blame upon you after what we have seen," because they had not seen among humans anyone resembling him or close to him. For he, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him, had been given half of beauty, as is established in the sound hadith of the Night Journey: that the Messenger of God ﷺ passed by Yusuf, peace be upon him, in the third heaven, and said: "Behold, he had been given half of beauty." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (162), from the hadith of Anas, may God be pleased with him.]]

Hammad ibn Salamah reported from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Yusuf and his mother were given half of beauty." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (16/80), al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/570), and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (5/385), through 'Affan from Hammad ibn Salamah. Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." Ibn 'Adi said: "I know of no one who raised this hadith to the Prophet except 'Affan; others stopped it at Hammad ibn Salamah. 'Affan is more famous, more trustworthy and more truthful than to be accused of anything that is attributed to weakness."]]

Sufyan al-Thawri reported from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud who said: Yusuf and his mother were given a third of beauty.

Abu Ishaq also said, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah: "The face of Yusuf was like lightning, and when a woman came to him for a need, he would cover his face, fearing that she would be tempted by him."

Al-Hasan al-Basri narrated it as a mursal report (one in which the Companion is omitted) from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Yusuf and his mother were given a third of the beauty of the people of this world, and people were given two-thirds" — or he said: "Yusuf and his mother were given two-thirds, and people were given a third." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (16/80).]]

Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Suhayli said: its meaning is that Yusuf had half the beauty of Adam, peace be upon him, for God created Adam with His own hand in the most perfect and most beautiful form, and there was none among his descendants who equalled him in beauty, and Yusuf had been given half of his beauty.

﴿This is nothing but a noble angel.﴾ She said: ﴿That is the one about whom you blamed me﴾. She says this as an excuse to them, that he deserves to be loved for his beauty and perfection.

﴿I did seek to seduce him from himself, but he refused﴾, i.e., he abstained. Some said: when they saw his outward beauty, she informed them of his good inner qualities which were hidden from them, namely chastity along with this beauty. Then she threatened: ﴿And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned and will surely be among the humiliated.﴾ At that point Yusuf, peace be upon him, sought refuge in God from their evil and their plotting, and said: ﴿My Lord, prison is dearer to me than that to which they invite me﴾, i.e., than immorality. ﴿And unless You turn away from me their plotting, I may incline toward them﴾, i.e., if You leave me to myself, then I have no power of my own, and I possess no harm or benefit for myself except by Your power and strength. You are the one sought for help, and upon You is reliance, so do not leave me to myself.

﴿I may incline toward them and be among the ignorant.﴾ So his Lord answered him: ﴿and turned away from him their plotting. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ This was because God, peace be upon him, granted Yusuf a great protection, guarded him and shielded him, so he refused her most firmly and chose prison over that. This is at the utmost level of perfection: that despite his youth, beauty and excellence, his mistress, who was the wife of the Governor of Egypt, invited him, and despite her extreme beauty, wealth and rank, he refused that and chose prison instead, out of fear of God and hope for His reward.

[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1423), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1031), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him.]]

Shaghaf is its covering.

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Shaghaf is love that kills, and shaghaf is less than that. Al-shaghaf is the veil of the heart."

﴿Indeed, we see her in clear error﴾, i.e., in this act of hers, of loving her young man and seeking to seduce him into herself.

﴿When she heard of their scheming﴾. Some said: "Of their words." Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "Rather, the news of Yusuf's beauty reached them, so they wished to see him, and they said that in order to find a way to see him and look at him. At that point, ﴿she sent for them﴾, i.e., she invited them to her house to entertain them, ﴿and prepared for them a mutaka'﴾."

Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Suddi and others said: it is the prepared gathering, in which there are cushions, pillows and food, including things that are cut with knives, such as citron and the like. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and she gave each one of them a knife﴾. This was a stratagem on her part and a counter to their own scheming to see him. ﴿And she said: "Come out before them"﴾, for she had hidden him in another place. ﴿When﴾ he came out and ﴿they saw him, they magnified him﴾, i.e., they greatly exalted his status and esteemed his rank, and they began to cut their hands in bewilderment at seeing him, thinking they were cutting the citron with the knives. The meaning is that they gashed their hands with them, as stated by more than one scholar.

It is also reported from Mujahid and Qatadah: they cut their hands until they threw them away. And God knows best.

It has been mentioned from Zayd ibn Aslam that she said to them, after they had eaten and their souls were content, and after she had placed citron before them and given each one of them a knife: "Would you like to look at Yusuf?" So it seems that they—and Allah knows best—imprisoned him only when the talk spread, falsely (ihāman, in one copy "ittihāman"), that this man had solicited her to herself, and that they imprisoned him on account of that. For this reason, when the great king requested him at the end of the period, he refused to leave until his innocence was established regarding what had been attributed to him of betrayal. When that was settled, he came out with his honor unblemished, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

As-Suddi said: The reason the king imprisoned them was that he suspected they had conspired to poison his food and drink.

Yusuf, peace be upon him, had become renowned in the prison for his generosity, trustworthiness, truthfulness, good bearing, and abundant worship, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, as well as for his knowledge of interpreting dreams, his kindness toward the people of the prison, visiting their sick, and fulfilling their rights. When these two young men entered the prison, they became attached to him and loved him intensely, and they said to him: "By Allah, we have come to love you with exceeding love." He said: "May Allah bless you both. Indeed, no one loves me without harm entering upon me because of that love. My aunt loved me, and harm befell me because of her; my father loved me, and I was harmed because of him; and the wife of the Aziz loved me, and it was likewise." They said: "By Allah, we cannot do otherwise than this."

Ikrimah said: He said, "I saw in what the sleeper sees that I planted a vine, and it grew, and clusters came out on it, so I pressed them and gave the king to drink." He said: "You will remain in the prison for three days, then you will come out and give him wine to drink."

The other, who was the baker, said: ﴿Indeed I see myself carrying upon my head bread, from which the birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed we see you as one of the good-doers﴾.
