Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 12, verses 37–38:

Yusuf (peace be upon him) informs the two of them that whatever dream they see in their sleep, he has knowledge of its interpretation (tafsir) and tells them its meaning (ta'wil) before it comes to pass. This is why he said: ﴿No food will come to you as your provision except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you.﴾

Mujahid said: He means, ﴿No food will come to you as your provision [in your sleep]﴾ ﴿except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you.﴾ As-Suddi said the same.

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yazid, a shaykh of his, narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Thawban, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I do not know, perhaps Yusuf (peace be upon him) used to abstain (ya'taf) from food while he was in this state, because I find in the Book of Allah, when he said to the two men: ﴿No food will come to you as your provision except that I will inform you of its interpretation,﴾ that when food came to him, sweet or bitter, he would abstain from it at that moment." Then Ibn Abbas said: "He was only taught, so he learned." This is a strange report (athar).

Then [Yusuf] said: This knowledge is only from Allah's teaching me, because I have forsaken the creed (millah) of the disbelievers in Allah and the Last Day, who do not hope for reward or punishment in the return. ﴿And I have followed the creed of my forefathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub.﴾ He means: I have abandoned the path of disbelief and polytheism, and I have taken the path of these messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all. This is the condition of whoever takes the path of guidance, follows the messengers and turns away from the path of the wrongdoers (al-zalimin). Indeed, He guides his heart, teaches him what he did not know, and makes him an imam to be followed in good, and a caller to the way of right guidance.

That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind.﴾ This is tawhid, which is the affirmation that there is no god but Him alone, without partner. ﴿From the bounty of Allah upon us﴾ means: He revealed it to us and commanded us with it. ﴿And upon mankind﴾ means: because He made us callers to it for them. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾ That is, they do not recognize the favor of Allah upon them in sending messengers to them. Rather, ﴿they have exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin.﴾ [Ibrahim: 28]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, that he used to treat the grandfather (jadd) as a father, and would say: "By Allah, whoever wishes, I will invoke a curse upon him at al-Hijr; Allah did not mention a grandfather or a grandmother." Allah, exalted is He, said, referring to the report about Yusuf: ﴿And I have followed the creed of my forefathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub.﴾

Rather, ﴿they have exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin.﴾ [Ibrahim: 28]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, that he used to treat the grandfather (jadd) as a father, and would say: "By Allah, whoever wishes, I will invoke a curse upon him at al-Hijr; Allah did not mention a grandfather or a grandmother." Allah, exalted is He, said, referring to the report about Yusuf: ﴿And I have followed the creed of my forefathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub.﴾

Then Yusuf, peace be upon him, turned to the two young men with address and invitation, calling them to worship Allah alone, without partner, and to renounce whatever else they worshipped of the idols which their people revered. He said: ﴿Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Irresistible?﴾

[That is] the One who subdues every thing by the might of His majesty and the greatness of His dominion.

Then he made clear to them that what they worship and name as gods is nothing but ignorance on their part, and a naming invented by themselves, which they received from their predecessors, and for which there is no basis from Allah. Therefore He said: ﴿Allah has sent down no authority for them﴾, meaning, no proof or evidence.

Then he informed them that judgment, disposal, will and dominion are all for Allah, and He has commanded all His servants without exception that they worship none but Him. Then he said: ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, meaning this to which I call you, of the Oneness of Allah and sincerity of deed toward Him, is the straight religion, which Allah commanded and sent down with clear proof and evidence, which He loves and is pleased with. ﴿But most people do not know﴾, meaning, for this reason most of them are polytheists. ﴿And most people, even if you were eager, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103].

Ibn Jurayj said: Yusuf only turned them away from the interpretation of the dream to this because he knew it would harm one of them, so he wished to occupy them with other than that, lest they return to him about it; but they returned to him, so he repeated the admonition to them. [Tafsir al-Tabari (16/102).]

There is consideration in what he said, because he had already promised them the interpretation at first. Rather, he made their question, in the manner of honour and respect, a means and a cause for calling them to Tawhid and Islam, because of what he saw in their disposition of accepting good, turning towards it, and listening to it. For this reason, when he finished calling them, he proceeded to interpret their dream, without repeating the question, saying:

He said: ﴿Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Irresistible?﴾

He says to them both: ﴿O my two fellow prisoners, as for one of you, he will give his lord wine to drink﴾. This is the one who had seen himself pressing wine. But he did not specify him, so that the other would not be grieved. For this reason he left him unspecified in his words: ﴿As for the other, he will be crucified, and birds will eat from his head﴾. This was the one who had seen himself carrying bread on his head.

Then he informed them that this matter had been decided and was certain to happen, because a dream follows the leg of a bird for as long as it is not interpreted. Once it is interpreted, it comes to pass.

Al-Thawri (Sufyan al-Thawri) said, from Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i), from Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), who said: "When the two of them said what they said, and he informed them, they said, 'We saw nothing.' He said: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire﴾."

Muhammad ibn Fudayl [[In (manuscript) T: "Fadl".]] narrated it from Umarah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud with the same wording. Likewise Mujahid, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others explained it. The essence of this is that whoever dreams a false dream and interprets it is bound by his own interpretation. And Allah knows best.

It has also been related in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, from Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "A dream follows the leg of a bird for as long as it is not interpreted [[In (manuscript) T: "yu'abbar".]]; once it is interpreted, it comes to pass." [[Its takhrij has already been mentioned in the commentary on verse "5" of this surah.]]

In the Musnad (a collection of hadiths arranged by the first narrator) of Abu Ya'la, through the route of Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "A dream belongs to the first one who interprets it." [[Ibn Majah also narrated it in his Sunan, no. (3915), through the route of Abdullah ibn Numayr, from al-A'mash, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, as a statement of Anas (mawquf). Al-Busayri said in al-Zawa'id (3/216): "This chain contains Yazid, who is weak."]]

When Yusuf (peace be upon him) assumed the deliverance of one of the two—namely the cupbearer—he said to him, secretly from the other, and Allah knows best, so that he would not make him aware that he was the one to be crucified: "Mention me to your lord" (﴿اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾). He means: mention my story to your lord—and he is the king—so the one entrusted with that forgot to remind his master of it. This was among the schemes of Shaytan, so that the Prophet of Allah would not emerge from the prison.

The correct view is that the pronoun in His words, ﴿فَأَنْسَاهُ الشَّيْطَانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ﴾ ("Shaytan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord"), refers to the one who was saved, as Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others said. It is also said that the pronoun refers to Yusuf (peace be upon him), as narrated by Ibn Jarir from Ibn Abbas, and also from Mujahid, Ikrimah and others. Here Ibn Jarir cited a hadith, saying:

Ibn WakI' narrated to us: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Had he not said that word—meaning Yusuf—he would not have remained in the prison as long as he did, for he sought relief from other than Allah."

This hadith is extremely weak, because Sufyan ibn WakI' is weak, and Ibrahim ibn Yazid—he is al-Khuzi—is weaker than him. It has been narrated from al-Hasan and Qatadah as mursal reports, each from one of them, and these mursal reports are not accepted here, even if mursal reports are accepted in other contexts. And Allah knows best.

As for "al-bid'" (بِضْع), Mujahid and Qatadah said: it is what is between three and nine. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Ayyub remained in affliction for seven years, Yusuf remained in prison for seven years, and the punishment of Bukhtunassar lasted seven years.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "He remained in the prison for a few years (بِضْعَ سِنِينَ)": he said twelve years. Al-Dahhak also said: fourteen years.

This dream of the king of Egypt was among the things God had decreed as the cause of Yusuf's release from prison, honored and dignified. The king saw this dream, and it disturbed him and amazed him, both regarding its matter and what its interpretation would be. So he gathered the soothsayers (kahanah), the diviners (hazzah), the grandees of his state, and his commanders, and related to them what he had seen. He asked them about its interpretation, but they did not know it. They excused themselves to him, saying that this was ﴿confused dreams﴾, meaning jumbled mixtures that had produced this dream of yours. ﴿We are not versed in the interpretation of dreams﴾, meaning: even if it were a true dream and not a confused mixture, we would still have no knowledge of its interpretation, which is its explanation (ta'wil).

At that point, the one of the two young men who had been in prison with Yusuf and had been saved remembered. Satan had caused him to forget what Yusuf had charged him with, namely mentioning his case to the king. So at that point he remembered, ﴿after a time﴾, meaning after a period. Some of them recited it as "ba'da ummatin" (بَعْدَ أَمِةٍ), meaning after forgetfulness. He said to the king and to those he had gathered for this matter: ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation﴾, meaning the interpretation of this dream, ﴿so send me forth﴾, meaning: dispatch me to Yusuf the truthful (al-Siddiq) in prison.

The meaning of the speech is that they sent him, and he came. He said: ﴿Yusuf, O truthful one, give us an interpretation﴾, and he mentioned the dream the king had seen. At that point Yusuf, peace be upon him, gave its interpretation to him without rebuking that young man for his forgetfulness of what he had charged him with, and without making his release conditional on anything beforehand. Rather he said: ﴿You will sow for seven years in succession﴾, meaning, when abundance and rain come to you for seven consecutive years. He interpreted the cows as years, because they plough the land from which fruits and crops are obtained, and these are the green ears of grain. Then he guided them to what they should rely upon in those years, saying: ﴿What you harvest, leave in its ear, except a little of what you eat﴾, meaning: whatever you gain from the abundance of these seven years, store it in its ears so that it remains preserved longer and is further from swift spoilage, except for the amount you eat. Let that be little by little, and do not be extravagant with it, so that you may benefit in the seven hard years. These are the seven years of dearth that follow these seven in succession, and they are the lean cows that devour the fat ones, because in years of barrenness what was gathered in years of abundance is consumed. These are the dried-up ears.

He informed them that these years would not produce anything, and that whatever they sowed in them would bring them no return. Therefore He said: ﴿They will consume what you have stored for them, except a little of what you keep back﴾.

Then, after the consecutive years of dearth, he gave them good news that there would follow them ﴿a year in which the people will be given rain﴾, meaning rain will come to them, the land will yield its produce, and people will press what they used to press as usual, such as oil and the like, and sugar and the like. To the point that some of them said: this also includes milking milk.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and in it they will press﴾: they will milk.

The king saw this dream, and it disturbed him and amazed him, both regarding its matter and what its interpretation would be. So he gathered the soothsayers (kahanah), the diviners (hazzah), the grandees of his state, and his commanders, and related to them what he had seen. He asked them about its interpretation, but they did not know it. They excused themselves to him, saying that this was ﴿confused dreams﴾, meaning jumbled mixtures that had produced this dream of yours. ﴿We are not versed in the interpretation of dreams﴾, meaning: even if it were a true dream and not a confused mixture, we would still have no knowledge of its interpretation, which is its explanation (ta'wil).

At that point, the one of the two young men who had been in prison with Yusuf and had been saved remembered. Satan had caused him to forget what Yusuf had charged him with, namely mentioning his case to the king. So at that point he remembered, ﴿after a time﴾, meaning after a period. Some of them recited it as "ba'da ummatin" (بَعْدَ أَمِةٍ), meaning after forgetfulness. He said to the king and to those he had gathered for this matter: ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation﴾, meaning the interpretation of this dream, ﴿so send me forth﴾, meaning: dispatch me to Yusuf the truthful (al-Siddiq) in prison.

The meaning of the speech is that they sent him, and he came. He said: ﴿Yusuf, O truthful one, give us an interpretation﴾, and he mentioned the dream the king had seen. At that point Yusuf, peace be upon him, gave its interpretation to him without rebuking that young man for his forgetfulness of what he had charged him with, and without making his release conditional on anything beforehand. Rather he said: ﴿You will sow for seven years in succession﴾, meaning, when abundance and rain come to you for seven consecutive years. He interpreted the cows as years, because they plough the land from which fruits and crops are obtained, and these are the green ears of grain. Then he guided them to what they should rely upon in those years, saying: ﴿What you harvest, leave in its ear, except a little of what you eat﴾, meaning: whatever you gain from the abundance of these seven years, store it in its ears so that it remains preserved longer and is further from swift spoilage, except for the amount you eat. Let that be little by little, and do not be extravagant with it, so that you may benefit in the seven hard years. These are the seven years of dearth that follow these seven in succession, and they are the lean cows that devour the fat ones, because in years of barrenness what was gathered in years of abundance is consumed. These are the dried-up ears.

He informed them that these years would not produce anything, and that whatever they sowed in them would bring them no return. Therefore He said: ﴿They will consume what you have stored for them, except a little of what you keep back﴾.

Then, after the consecutive years of dearth, he gave them good news that there would follow them ﴿a year in which the people will be given rain﴾, meaning rain will come to them, the land will yield its produce, and people will press what they used to press as usual, such as oil and the like, and sugar and the like. To the point that some of them said: this also includes milking milk.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and in it they will press﴾: they will milk.

Allah the Exalted says, reporting about the king when they returned to him with the interpretation of his dream, which he had seen, [the interpretation] that pleased him and reassured him. Thus he recognized the excellence of Yusuf, peace be upon him, his knowledge, his good understanding of his dream, and his good character among those in his land who were his subjects. So he said: ﴿Bring him to me﴾, meaning: take him out of the prison and bring him here. When the messenger came to him with that, he refused to leave until the king and his subjects had established his innocence and the purity of his honour from what had been attributed to him concerning the wife of al-'Aziz, and that this imprisonment had not been for any matter that warranted it, but was rather injustice and aggression. So he said: ﴿Return to your lord and ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot﴾.

The Sunnah has also come praising him for this, and drawing attention to his excellence, his nobility, the loftiness of his rank, and his patience, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. In the Musnad (a collection of hadith arranged by the narrators' names) and the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), from the narration of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id and Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We have more right to doubt than Ibrahim, when he said: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said, 'Have you not believed?' He said, 'Yes, but [I ask] that my heart may be assured﴾ [al-Baqarah: 260]. May Allah have mercy on Lut; he used to take refuge in a strong pillar. And had I remained in prison as long as Yusuf remained, I would have answered the caller."¹

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying: ﴿Ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands. 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been amazed at Yusuf, at his patience and his generosity, and may Allah forgive him, when he was asked about the lean cows and the fat ones. And if I had been in his place, I would not have answered them until I stipulated that they bring me out. And I have been amazed at Yusuf, at his patience and his generosity, and may Allah forgive him, when the messenger came to him. If I had been in his place, I would have rushed to the door, but he wanted to have the excuse."³ This is a mursal hadith (one in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "What was your affair when you sought to seduce Yusuf from himself?"﴾ is a report about the king when he gathered the women who had cut their hands at the house of the wife of al-'Aziz. He addressed all of them, while he meant the wife of his minister, who was al-'Aziz: ﴿What was your affair﴾, meaning: what was your matter and your news ﴿when you sought to seduce Yusuf from himself﴾, meaning: on the day of the banquet? ﴿They said, "Allah forbid! We know of him no evil."﴾ Meaning: the women replied to the king: Allah forbid that Yusuf should be accused, and by Allah, we know of him no evil. At that point ﴿the wife of al-'Aziz said, "Now the truth has come to light."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: she means, "Now the truth has become clear, manifest, and apparent."

﴿I was the one who sought to seduce him from himself, and indeed, he is of the truthful﴾, meaning: in his saying: ﴿She sought to seduce me from myself﴾. ﴿That [He did so] so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾. It has also been said that this is from the speech of Yusuf, peace be upon him, from his saying: ﴿That [He did so] so that he may know that I did not betray him﴾, concerning his wife, ﴿in his absence﴾, the two verses, meaning: I only sent back the messenger so that the king would know my innocence and so that al-'Aziz would know that I did not betray him concerning his wife in his absence. ﴿And that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers. We know of him no evil." The wife of al-'Aziz said, "Now the truth has come to light. I was the one who sought to seduce him from himself, and indeed, he is of the truthful."﴾ Yusuf said: ﴿That [He did so] so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, [and that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers]﴾. He said: Then Jibril, peace be upon him, said to him: "Nor on the day you resolved to do what you resolved." So he said: ﴿And I do not acquit myself; indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil﴾.⁵

This is also what Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi said. 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been amazed at Yusuf, at his patience and his generosity, and may Allah forgive him, when he was asked about the lean cows and the fat ones. And if I had been in his place, I would not have answered them until I stipulated that they bring me out. And I have been amazed at Yusuf, at his patience and his generosity, and may Allah forgive him, when the messenger came to him. If I had been in his place, I would have rushed to the door, but he wanted to have the excuse."³ This is a mursal hadith (one in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "What was your affair when you sought to seduce Yusuf from himself?"﴾ is a report about the king when he gathered the women who had cut their hands at the house of the wife of al-'Aziz. He addressed all of them, while he meant the wife of his minister, who was al-'Aziz: ﴿What was your affair﴾, meaning: what was your matter and your news ﴿when you sought to seduce Yusuf from himself﴾, meaning: on the day of the banquet? ﴿They said, "Allah forbid! We know of him no evil."﴾ Meaning: the women replied to the king: Allah forbid that Yusuf should be accused, and by Allah, we know of him no evil. At that point ﴿the wife of al-'Aziz said, "Now the truth has come to light."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: she means, "Now the truth has become clear, manifest, and apparent."

﴿I was the one who sought to seduce him from himself, and indeed, he is of the truthful﴾, meaning: in his saying: ﴿She sought to seduce me from myself﴾. ﴿That [He did so] so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾. She says: I have only confessed this against myself so that my husband may know that I did not betray him in reality, and the greatest prohibited act did not occur. I merely pursued this young man with solicitation, but he refused. Therefore I have confessed so that he may know that I am innocent. ﴿And that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers. And I do not acquit myself; indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil﴾. The woman says: "I do not acquit myself, for the soul speaks to itself and desires; that is why I solicited him, for it commands to evil." ﴿Except those upon whom my Lord has mercy﴾, meaning: except those whom Allah the Exalted protects. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

This statement is the most widely known, the most fitting, and the most consistent with the context of the story and the meanings of the speech. Al-Mawardi related it in his tafsir, and the eminent scholar Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, undertook to defend it and devoted to it a separate work.⁴

It has also been said that this is from the speech of Yusuf, peace be upon him, from his saying: ﴿That [He did so] so that he may know that I did not betray him﴾, concerning his wife, ﴿in his absence﴾, the two verses, meaning: I only sent back the messenger so that the king would know my innocence and so that al-'Aziz would know that I did not betray him concerning his wife in his absence. ﴿And that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers. And I do not acquit myself; indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil﴾, [the verse]. This is the view that neither Ibn Jarir nor Ibn Abi Hatim related other than.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the king gathered the women and asked them: "Did you seek to seduce Yusuf from himself?" ﴿They said, "Allah forbid! We know of him no evil." The wife of al-'Aziz said, "Now the truth has come to light. I was the one who sought to seduce him from himself, and indeed, he is of the truthful."﴾ Yusuf said: ﴿That [He did so] so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, [and that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers]﴾. He said: Then Jibril, peace be upon him, said to him: "Nor on the day you resolved to do what you resolved." So he said: ﴿And I do not acquit myself; indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil﴾.⁵

This is also what Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi said. However, the first view is stronger and more evident, because the whole context of the speech is from the speech of the wife of al-'Aziz in the presence of the king, and Yusuf, peace be upon him, was not among them, but only after that did the king bring him in.

As-Suddi, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others among the commentators (mufassirun) mentioned that the reason which brought the brothers of Yusuf to the land of Egypt was that when Yusuf, peace be upon him, took up the office of vizier in Egypt, and the seven fruitful years passed, then came years of drought, and famine spread throughout the whole land of Egypt and reached the land of Kan'an (Canaan), where Ya'qub (Jacob), peace be upon him, and his sons were. At that time Yusuf, peace be upon him, took precautions for the people regarding their harvests, and gathered them in the best possible way. A great amount was thereby obtained, and enormous, vast granaries. People came to him from all the regions and places of dealing, seeking grain for themselves and their dependants. A man was not given more than one camel-load per year. Yusuf, peace be upon him, did not satisfy himself fully, and neither he nor the king and his soldiers ate except one meal at midday, so that the people would be sufficient with what was in their hands for the period of seven years. And this was a mercy from Allah upon the people of Egypt.

As for what some commentators have mentioned, that he sold them in the first year for money, in the second for goods, in the third for such-and-such, and in the fourth for such-and-such, until he sold them themselves and their children after he had taken possession of all that they owned, then freed them and returned to them all their property, Allah knows best the soundness of that. It is among the Isra'iliyyat (narratives taken from Jewish and Christian sources) which are neither confirmed nor denied.

The point is that among those who came to obtain grain was a group of the brothers of Yusuf, by their father's command to them in this matter. It had reached them that the ʿAziz of Egypt was giving people food in exchange for payment, so they took with them merchandise with which to exchange for food. Ten men rode out, and Ya'qub, peace be upon him, held back with him Binyamin, the full brother of Yusuf, peace be upon them both, and he was the dearest of his sons to him after Yusuf. When they entered upon Yusuf, while he was sitting in his majesty, his authority and his lordship, he recognised them when he looked at them, ﴿but they did not recognise him﴾, meaning they did not know him, because they had parted from him when he was a small youth, and they had sold him to a caravan, and they did not know where they were taking him, nor did they imagine that he would come to what he came to. Therefore they did not recognise him, whereas he recognised them.

As-Suddi and others mentioned that he began to address them, saying to them, as one who disapproves of them: "What has brought you to my land?" They said: "O ʿAziz, we have come for grain." He said: "Perhaps you are spies?" They said: "We seek refuge in Allah!" He said: "From where are you?" They said: "From the land of Kan'an, and our father Ya'qub is a prophet of Allah." He said: "And does he have sons other than you?" They said: "Yes. We were twelve; our youngest went away and perished in the wilderness, and he was the dearest of us to his father. His full brother remained, and his father held him back so as to console himself with him for the other." So he ordered that they be lodged and honoured.

﴿When he had furnished them with their provisions﴾, meaning he fulfilled their measure for them and loaded their camels with their loads, he said: "Bring me your brother of whom you have spoken, so that I may know the truth of what you have said. Then he frightened them, saying: ﴿But if you do not bring him to me, then there shall be no measure for you with me, nor shall you come near me.﴾ That is, if you do not bring him with you on the second occasion, then you shall have no grain from me. They said: ﴿We will seek to persuade his father concerning him, and we will certainly do it.﴾ That is, we will strive to bring him to you by every possible means, and we will spare no effort, so that you may know the truth of what we have said.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 12, verse 69:

It is related by the Most High concerning the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) when they came before Yusuf, and with them was his full brother Binyamin (Benjamin). So he brought them into the house of his honour and the abode of his hospitality, and he showered upon them gifts, kindness and generosity. Then he took his brother aside privately, informed him of his own situation and what had befallen him, and made him aware that he was his brother. He said to him: ﴿Do not grieve﴾, that is, do not be distressed over what they did to me. He commanded him to keep this hidden from them, and not to let them know what he had told him, namely that he was his brother. And he agreed with him that he would devise a plan to keep him with himself, honoured, esteemed and revered.

When he had equipped them with their provisions, he placed the drinking-cup (al-siqayah) in his brother's bag. It is, according to most scholars, a cup of silver. It was also said to be of gold; this was reported by Ibn Zayd. He used to drink from it, and he would measure out grain to the people with it when food was scarce at that time. This was reported by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿the measure of the king﴾, that he said: "It was of silver, and they drank from it. It was like a mikkuk (a measuring vessel), and al-'Abbas had one like it in the Jahiliyyah. So he placed it in Benjamin's baggage without anyone noticing. Then a caller called out among them: ﴿O caravan, you are surely thieves!﴾ They turned toward the caller and said: ﴿What is it that you are missing?﴾ They said: ﴿We are missing the measure of the king,﴾ meaning his measuring vessel with which he measures, ﴿and for whoever brings it is a camel's load,﴾ and this is from the category of ju'alah (a reward-contract), ﴿and I guarantee it.﴾ This is from the category of ḍamān (surety) and kafālah (guarantee)."

By the Lord, you know well that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and that we were never thieves. [[In T: "mudh" (since).]] That is, you have certainly been certain of it and have known it since you first became acquainted with us, because they had witnessed from them good conduct: that we did not come to spread corruption in the land and were not thieves. That is, our natural disposition does not require this characteristic.

The young men said to them: "What is the penalty for it," meaning for the thief, "if you are liars?" That is, what would be the punishment for it if we find it among you, [[In A: "whoever took it among them"]]?

They said: "Its penalty is that whoever is found in his saddlebag, he himself is its penalty. Thus do We requite the wrongdoers."

This was the law (shari'ah) of Abraham: that a thief is handed over to the one from whom he stole. This is what Yusuf, peace be upon him, intended. For this reason he began with their bags before his brother's bag, that is, he searched them before him, as a stratagem (tawriyah, a concealment of intent through an ambiguous expression), "then he brought it out from his brother's bag." So he took him from them by virtue of their own confession and commitment, and as an obligation upon them according to what they themselves believed. For this reason the Exalted said: "Thus did We devise for Yusuf." This is among the praiseworthy stratagems that Allah loves and is pleased with, because of the wisdom and the sought-after benefit it contains.

* *

As for His saying: "He could not have taken his brother under the king's law," that is, he had no right to seize him under the ruling of the king of Egypt, as said by al-Dahhak and others.

Allah only facilitated for him that his brothers bound themselves to what they had bound themselves to, and he knew this from their law. For this reason the Exalted praised him, saying: "We raise in degrees whom We will." As the Exalted said: "Allah will raise those among you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees, and Allah is Aware of what you do" [al-Mujadilah: 11].

"And above every possessor of knowledge is one who knows." Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "No scholar exists but that above him is a scholar, until it ends with Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Similarly, Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abd al-A'la al-Tha'labi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "We were with Ibn Abbas when he related a wondrous narration, and a man marvelled at it and said: 'Praise be to Allah, above every possessor of knowledge is one who knows.' [Ibn Abbas said: 'Evil is what you have said. Allah is the All-Knowing, and He is above every scholar.']" Similarly, Simak narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "And above every possessor of knowledge is one who knows": "This one is more knowing than that one, and that one is more knowing than this one, and Allah is above every scholar." Likewise Ikrimah said.

Qatadah said: "And above every possessor of knowledge is one who knows," until knowledge ends with Allah. From Him it began, and the scholars learned from Him, and to Him it returns. In the reading of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it is: "And above every scholar is one who knows."

And the brothers of Joseph said, when they saw the drinking-cup had been taken out of Benjamin's belongings: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before.﴾ They were clearing themselves before the Ruler of being associated with him, and mentioning that this one did what a brother of his before him did, meaning Joseph, peace be upon him.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Qatadah: Joseph had stolen an idol belonging to his grandfather, his mother's father, and broke it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The first trial that befell Joseph, as it has reached me, was that his paternal aunt, the daughter of Isaac, who was Isaac's eldest child, had the girdle of Isaac with her, and they would inherit it by seniority. Whoever among them held it, from among those who were in charge of it, had a sole right to it that no one disputed, and he would do with it as he wished. When Jacob's son Joseph was born, his aunt had raised him, so he belonged to her and she to him. No one loved anything as much as she loved him. When he grew up and reached several years of age, Jacob's heart became attached to him, so he came to her and said: "O sister, hand Joseph over to me, for by God I cannot bear for him to be away from me for an hour." She said: "By God, I will not leave him." Then she said: "Leave him with me for some days, that I may look at him and be comforted about him, perhaps that will console me for him," or as she said. When Jacob had left her, she took Isaac's girdle and tied it around Joseph beneath his clothes. Then she said: "The girdle of Isaac, peace be upon him, has been lost. Look for whoever took it and whoever has it." They searched, and then she said: "Search the members of the household." They searched them and found it with Joseph. She said: "By God, he is mine to keep, and I may do with him as I wish." Jacob came to her and she told him the news. He said to her: "It is up to you. If he did that, then he is yours to keep; I can do nothing other than that." So she held on to him, and Jacob could not get him back until she died. He said: So this is what the brothers of Joseph meant when Joseph was treated as he was treated when he was taken: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before.﴾ [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (16/196).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So Joseph kept it hidden within himself﴾, meaning: the statement that follows it, which is His saying: ﴿You are worse in position, and God knows best what you describe,﴾ that is, what you mention. He said this within himself and did not reveal it to them. This is of the type of pronoun placed before its referent (al-idmar qabl al-dhikr), which is common, like the saying of the poet:

His sons repaid Abu al-Ghaylan for his old age ... and for good conduct, as Sinimmar was repaid.

The poet is Sulayt ibn Sa'd, and the verse is among the evidences cited by Ibn Aqil in his commentary on Ibn Malik's Alfiyya, number (153).

There are many examples of this in the Qur'an, the Hadith and the language, in its prose, its reports and its poetry.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿So Joseph kept it hidden within himself﴾: he kept hidden within himself: ﴿You are worse in position, and God knows best what you describe.﴾

When the seizure of Benjamin was settled and his detention with Joseph was established by their own admission, they began to plead with him and appeal to his compassion. So ﴿They said, "O Aziz, indeed he has an aged father, a very old man, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you are among the good-doers."﴾ They meant: he loves him with an intense love and consoles himself with him for the son he lost. ﴿So take one of us in his place﴾, i.e., instead of him, to remain with you as a substitute for him. ﴿Indeed, we see you are among the good-doers﴾ [[In A: "lanaraka" (indeed we see you), which is an error.]], i.e., among the just, the fair, and those receptive to goodness.

﴿He said, "We seek refuge in Allah from taking anyone except the one with whom we found our property"﴾, i.e., as you yourselves said and acknowledged. ﴿Indeed, then we would be wrongdoers﴾ [[Addition from T, A.]] [أَيْ] if we seized an innocent man in place of the guilty one.

Ibn Kathir said, concerning the brothers of Yusuf: When they despaired of freeing their brother Binyamin, whom they had bound themselves to their father to return to him and had sworn to him on that, and this was prevented from them, ﴿they withdrew﴾, that is, they separated from the people ﴿in private consultation﴾, conferring among themselves.

﴿The eldest of them said﴾, and he was Ruben. It was also said he was Yahuda, and he is the one who had advised them to cast him into the well when they resolved to kill him. He said to them: ﴿Do you not know that your father has taken an oath from you in the name of Allah﴾ that you would bring him back to him? ﴿You have seen how it became impossible for you, along with what you previously committed of losing Yusuf from him. So I will not leave this land﴾, that is, I will not depart from this town, ﴿until my father gives me permission﴾ to return to him, being pleased with me, ﴿or Allah judges for me﴾. It was said: by the sword. It was also said: by enabling me to take my brother. ﴿And He is the best of judges.﴾ [[In manuscripts T and A: "ahkam al-hakimin" (the most judicious of judges), which is an error.]]

Then he ordered them to inform their father of the exact circumstances of what had happened, so that it would serve as an excuse for them before him, and that they would clear themselves to him and disown what had happened by their statement.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 12, verse 83–86:

He said to them as he had said to them when they came to him with Joseph's shirt stained with false blood: ﴿Rather, your souls have made a matter attractive to you, so patience is most fitting.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When they came to Ya'qub and informed him of what had happened, he suspected them, and thought that it was like their deed with Joseph. ﴿He said, "Rather, your souls have made a matter attractive to you, so patience is most fitting."﴾

Some people said: Since their present conduct was a consequence of their earlier deed, the earlier ruling was applied to it, and his statement ﴿Rather, your souls have made a matter attractive to you, so patience is most fitting﴾ was correct.

Then he hoped from Allah that He would return to him his three sons: Joseph, his brother Benjamin, and Rubil, who had stayed in the land of Egypt awaiting Allah's decree concerning him, either that his father would be pleased with him and order him to return to him, or that he would take his brother secretly. Therefore he said: ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring them all to me. Indeed, He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.﴾ That is, All-Knowing of my condition, All-Wise in His actions, His decree and His destiny.

﴿And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my grief over Joseph!"﴾ That is, he turned away from his sons and, recalling Joseph's former and original sorrow, said: ﴿Oh, my grief over Joseph!﴾ The grief of the two sons renewed for him the buried sorrow.

Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri informed us, from Sufyan al-'Usfuri, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said: No one other than this Ummah was given istirja' (the saying "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return"). Do you not hear the words of Ya'qub, peace be upon him: ﴿"Oh, my grief over Joseph!" and his eyes turned white from grief, and he was suppressing (his anger).﴾ That is, he was silent and did not complain of his matter to any creature. Qatadah and others said this.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿fa-huwa kazim﴾ means "one who is suppressing his grief and sorrowful."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah [narrated to us, Abu Musa], from Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed Dawud, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, the Children of Israel ask You by Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub, so make me the fourth of them. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: O Dawud, Ibrahim was thrown into the fire for My sake and he was patient, and that was a trial that did not reach you. Ishaq offered the essence of his blood for My sake and he was patient, and that was a trial that did not reach you. And Ya'qub had his beloved taken from him until his eyes turned white from grief, and he was patient, and that was a trial that did not reach you."

This is a mursal narration, and it contains a irregularity (nakarah); for the correct view is that Isma'il is the one who was to be sacrificed. Moreover, Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an has many unfamiliar and strange reports. And Allah knows best.

The closest explanation to this is that al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, may Allah have mercy on him, related it from some of the Children of Israel, such as Ka'b and Wahb and others like them, and Allah knows best. For the Israelites relate that when Ya'qub's son had been detained because of the theft, Ya'qub wrote to Yusuf, seeking to win his release and mentioning to him that they were a household afflicted with trials: Ibrahim was tested with the fire, Ishaq with the sacrifice, and Ya'qub with separation from Yusuf, in a long narration that is not authentic, and Allah knows best. At that point his sons felt pity for him, and they said to him, out of gentleness toward him and compassion for him: ﴿They said, "By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become fatigued (harad) or become among the perishing."﴾ That is, you will not stop remembering Joseph, ﴿until you become harad﴾ — weak of body and weak of strength — ﴿or become among the perishing﴾. They meant: if this state continues with you, we fear for you destruction and death.

﴿He said, "I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah."﴾ That is, he answered what they had said with his statement: ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief﴾, that is, my concern and what I am in, ﴿to Allah﴾ alone. ﴿And I know from Allah what you do not know﴾, that is, I hope from Him every good.

It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿And I know from Allah what you do not know﴾ [meaning: the dream of Joseph, that it is true, and that Allah will surely make it manifest and fulfil it. Al-'Awfi also related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And I know from Allah what you do not know﴾ — I know that Joseph's dream is true, and that I will indeed prostrate to him.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Ghaniyyah narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Umar ibn Abi al-Zubayr, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Prophet Ya'qub, peace be upon him, had a brother in faith (a close friend), who said to him one day: What took away your sight and bent your back? He said: What took away my sight is weeping over Joseph, and what bent my back is grief over Benjamin. Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and said: O Ya'qub, Allah sends you His greetings and says to you: Are you not ashamed to complain about Me to other than Me? Ya'qub said: I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah. Jibril, peace be upon him, said: Allah knows best what you complain of."

This is a strange narration, and it contains a irregularity.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 12, verses 87–88:

Allah, the Exalted, says, informing about Ya'qub (peace be upon him), that he urged his sons to go out into the land to seek news of Yusuf and his brother Binyamin.

Al-tahassus (searching for information) is used for good, while al-tajassus (spying) is used for evil.

He roused them, gave them good news, and commanded them not to despair of the mercy of Allah, meaning: do not cut off your hope and expectation from Allah regarding what you seek and aim for, for indeed none cuts off hope and despairs of Allah except the disbelieving people (﴿إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾).

* *

His saying, ﴿فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ﴾ (So when they entered upon him), the implied meaning is: they set out, entered the land of Egypt, and entered upon Yusuf. ﴿قَالُوا يَا أَيُّهَا الْعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهْلَنَا الضُّرُّ﴾ (They said, "O ruler, adversity has touched us and our family"), meaning from the drought, famine and scarcity of food. ﴿وَجِئْنَا بِبِضَاعَةٍ مُزْجَاةٍ﴾ (And we have come with meager merchandise), meaning: we have with us the price of the food you sell us, and it is a small price. This was said by Mujahid, al-Hasan, and others.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the inferior thing that is not accepted, such as the worn-out sack, the rope, and the like. In another report from him: it is the bad dirhams which are only accepted at a loss. Qatadah and al-Suddi said the same.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr [and Ikrimah] said: it is the worn dirhams (al-darahim al-fusul).

Abu Salih said: it is the pine nut (al-sanawbar) and the green seed (habbat al-khadra').

Al-Dahhak said: it is unsalable goods that are not accepted.

Abu Salih also said: they brought the green seeds of the terebinth (habb al-butm) and pine nuts.

The root meaning of al-izjaa' is pushing away because of the weakness of a thing, as Hatim al-Ta'i said:

"Let him weep over Milhan, a pushed-away guest,
And a widow who drives away with the night a widow."

And A'sha Banu Tha'labah said:

"The giver of a hundred white camels, and their herdsmen,
Pregnant she-camels driving their young before them."

* *

His saying, reporting about them: ﴿فَأَوْفِ لَنَا الْكَيْلَ﴾ (So give us full measure), meaning: give us, for this small price, what you used to give us before that. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "Fa-awqir rikabana wa tasaddaq 'alayna" (So fill our camels' loads and give us charity).

Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنَا﴾ (and be charitable to us) means by returning our brother to us.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: ﴿وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنَا﴾ means they are saying: be charitable to us by accepting this meager merchandise, and overlook its deficiency.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah was asked: Was charity forbidden to any of the prophets before the Prophet (ﷺ)? He said: Have you not heard His saying: ﴿فَأَوْفِ لَنَا الْكَيْلَ وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْزِي الْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ﴾ (So give us full measure and be charitable to us; indeed, Allah rewards the charitable)? Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Harith, from al-Qasim, from him.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to us, al-Qasim narrated to us, Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, who said: I heard Mujahid being asked: Is it disliked for a man to say in his supplication, "O Allah, be charitable to me"? He said: Yes, charity is only for one who seeks reward.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 12, verses 89–92:

Allah the Exalted says, reporting about Yusuf (peace be upon him): When his brothers mentioned to him the hardship and distress that had befallen them, the scarcity of food, and the widespread drought, and he remembered his father and the grief he was in over the loss of his two sons, together with his own kingship, authority and abundance, then tenderness, compassion, mercy and pity for his father and his brothers overcame him, and weeping burst forth from him. So he made himself known to them. It is said that he lifted the crown from his forehead, and there was a mole on it. And he said: ﴿Do you know what you did to Yusuf and his brother, when you were ignorant?﴾ That is, how they separated him from his brother. ﴿When you were ignorant﴾ means: what led you to this was only ignorance of the magnitude of what you committed, as one of the early generations (al-salaf) said: "Everyone who disobeys Allah is ignorant," and he recited: ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who do evil in ignorance, and then repent after that and make amends, indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nahl: 119].

And the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that Yusuf (peace be upon him) made himself known to them by himself, with Allah's permission for him to do so, just as he had concealed himself from them in the first two occasions by the command of Allah the Exalted to him in that matter, and Allah knows best. But when the situation became constricted and the matter grew severe, Allah the Exalted relieved that distress, as He said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾ [Ash-Sharh: 5–6]. At that point they said: ﴿Are you indeed Yusuf?﴾

Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited: "Aw anta Yusuf" (Or are you Yusuf?), and Ibn Muhaysin recited: "Innaka la-anta Yusuf" (Indeed you are Yusuf). The well-known recitation is the first, because the interrogative indicates astonishment, meaning: they marvelled at this, that they had been coming to him for two years or more, and they did not recognise him, while he recognised them and concealed himself. Therefore they said, in the form of a question: ﴿Are you indeed Yusuf?﴾ He said: ﴿I am Yusuf, and this is my brother. Allah has been gracious to us﴾, that is, by bringing us together after separation and after a long period. ﴿Indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient, then indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers.﴾ They said: ﴿By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us, and indeed we were sinners﴾, acknowledging to him his superiority and preference over them in form and character, in abundance and kingship, in authority, and also in prophethood according to the view of those who do not consider them prophets, and they confessed to him that they had wronged him and erred against him.

﴿He said: "No reproach be upon you today"﴾ means: no rebuke and no blame upon you today, and I will not hold your sin against me after today.

Then he added to it by praying for their forgiveness, saying: ﴿May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾

Al-Suddi said: They apologised to Yusuf, and he said: ﴿No reproach be upon you today﴾, meaning: I will not mention your sin to you.

Ibn Ishaq and al-Thawri said: ﴿No reproach be upon you [today]﴾ means: no rebuke shall be upon you today from me for what you did. ﴿May Allah forgive you﴾ means: may Allah conceal your deeds for you. ﴿And He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾

Ibn Kathir said, in his commentary on Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on surah 12, verses 99–100:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of the arrival of Ya'qub, peace be upon him, to Yusuf, peace be upon him, and of his coming to the land of [[In A: "upon".]] Egypt. Yusuf had instructed his brothers to bring all of their family to him, so they gathered up all of them, to the last one, and set out from the land of Canaan heading for the land of [[In T, A: "the domains of".]] Egypt. When Yusuf, peace be upon him, was informed of their approach, he went out to meet them, and [the king] [[Added from T, A.]] ordered his commanders and the notables of the people to go out [with Yusuf] [[Added from T, A.]] to receive the Prophet of Allah, Ya'qub, peace be upon him. It is also said that the king himself went out to receive him, and this is the more likely view.

The statement of Allah, ﴿He took his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in security."﴾ has been problematic for many of the exegetes [[In T: "many of".]]. Some of them said: this is an instance of inversion (al-muqaddam wa'l-mu'akhkhar), and the meaning of the speech is: ﴿"Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in security," and he took his parents to himself and raised them upon the throne.﴾

Ibn Jarir refuted this and was correct in doing so. Then he chose what he related from al-Suddi: that Yusuf took his parents to himself when he met them, and then, when they reached the gate of the city, he said: ﴿Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in security.﴾

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (1007), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Ibn Jarir said: no evidence has been established for the death of his mother, and the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that she was alive. This view which he supported is the one favored by the context.

* *

It is related in a hadith that Mu'adh came to Syria and found them prostrating to their bishops. When he returned, he prostrated to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "What is this, O Mu'adh?" He replied: "I saw them prostrating to their bishops, and you are more deserving that prostration be made to you, O Messenger of Allah." [[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/381) and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (1853), from the hadith of Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him; Ibn Hibban graded it sahih.]]

He said: "Do not prostrate to me, O Salman, but prostrate to the Living One who never dies." [[Narrated by Abu Nu'aym in Tarikh Isbahan (2/103) through the chain of Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Salman, may Allah be pleased with him; it will come at the commentary on verse 58 of surah al-Furqan.]]

On the day its ta'wil comes﴾ [al-A'raf: 53], that is, on the Day of Resurrection there will come to them what they were promised of good and evil.

He said: some say they were in al-Awlaj, on the side of a mountain pass below Hasma, and they were people of the desert, with sheep and camels.

﴿After Satan had incited discord between me and my brothers.﴾ [Then he said] [[Added from T, A.]] ﴿Indeed my Lord is Gentle with what He wills﴾, that is, when He wills a matter, He arranges means for it, facilitates it, and decrees it. ﴿Indeed He is the All-Knowing﴾ of the interests of His servants, ﴿the All-Wise﴾ in His actions and words, His decree and destiny, and in what He chooses and wills.

'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad said: and to it the farthest extent of dreams leads. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

[[Tafsir al-Tabari (1/273).]]

Qatadah said: there were thirty-five years between them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: it was mentioned, and Allah knows best, that Yusuf's absence from Ya'qub lasted eighteen years. He said: the People of the Book claim that it was forty years or about that, and that Ya'qub, peace be upon him, remained with Yusuf for seventeen years after he came to him in Egypt, and then Allah took him to Himself.

Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i said, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: the Children of Israel entered Egypt when they were seventy-three persons, and they left it when they were six hundred thousand and seventy thousand.

Abu Ishaq said, from Masruq: they entered when they were three hundred and ninety, men and women included. And Allah knows best.

Musa ibn 'Ubaydah said, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad: the family of Ya'qub gathered to Yusuf in Egypt, and they were eighty-six persons, young and old, male and female, and they left it as six hundred thousand and more.

Ibn Kathir said, in his commentary on Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on surah 12, verses 99–100:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of the arrival of Ya'qub, peace be upon him, to Yusuf, peace be upon him, and of his coming to the land of [[In A: "upon".]] Egypt. Yusuf had instructed his brothers to bring all of their family to him, so they gathered up all of them, to the last one, and set out from the land of Canaan heading for the land of [[In T, A: "the domains of".]] Egypt. When Yusuf, peace be upon him, was informed of their approach, he went out to meet them, and [the king] [[Added from T, A.]] ordered his commanders and the notables of the people to go out [with Yusuf] [[Added from T, A.]] to receive the Prophet of Allah, Ya'qub, peace be upon him. It is also said that the king himself went out to receive him, and this is the more likely view.

The statement of Allah, ﴿He took his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in security."﴾ has been problematic for many of the exegetes [[In T: "many of".]]. This is the supplication of Yusuf the Truthful (al-Siddiq), which he made to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, after his blessing was complete through his reunion with his parents and brothers, and after the favours Allah had bestowed on him of prophethood and kingship. He asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, that just as He had perfected His blessing upon him in this world, He would continue it for him in the Hereafter, that He would cause him to die as a Muslim when his death came, and that He would join him with the righteous, who are his brothers among the prophets and messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and upon them all. [[The words "upon him and" are an addition from manuscripts T and A.]] This is the view of al-Dahhak.

It is possible that Yusuf, peace be upon him, said this at the time of his death, as has been established in the two Sahihs from A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would raise his finger at the time of death and say: "O Allah, grant me the Highest Companion. O Allah, grant me the Highest Companion. O Allah, grant me the Highest Companion." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4437, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2444.]]

It is also possible that he asked for death upon Islam and for joining the righteous when his appointed time came and his life was over, not that he asked for it to be granted immediately, just as a person prays for another: "May Allah cause you to die upon Islam." And a person says: "O Allah, keep us alive as Muslims, cause us to die as Muslims, and join us with the righteous."

It is also possible that he asked for it to be granted immediately, and that this was permissible in their religious law, as Qatadah said regarding the verse ﴿Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous﴾: when Allah had gathered his family and comforted him, and he was then immersed in the world, its kingship and its plenty, he yearned for the righteous who had come before him. Ibn Abbas used to say: No prophet ever wished for death before Yusuf, peace be upon him.

Similarly, Ibn Jarir and al-Suddi reported from Ibn Abbas that he was the first prophet to pray with this supplication. It is possible that he was the first to ask for death upon Islam, just as Nuh was the first to say: ﴿My Lord, forgive me, my parents, and whoever enters my house as a believer﴾ [Nuh: 28]. It is also possible that he was the first to ask for it to be granted immediately, and this is the apparent meaning of Qatadah's context. However, this is not permissible in our Shari'ah (the revealed law, i.e. the religious law).

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you should wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him. If he must wish for death, let him say: 'O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is better for me, and cause me to die when death is better for me.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/101).]]

[It was also narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, and in their version: "None of you should wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him; if he is a doer of good, he may increase, and if he is a doer of evil, perhaps he will repent. But let him say: 'O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is better for me, and cause me to die when death is better for me.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6351, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2680.]]] [[An addition from manuscripts T and A.]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, Ali ibn Yazid narrated to me, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: We sat with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he admonished us and softened our hearts. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas wept greatly, and he said: "Would that I had died!" The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Sa'd, do you wish for death in my presence?" He repeated this three times [[An addition from manuscripts T and A, and the Musnad.]], and then said: "O Sa'd, if you were created for Paradise, then whether your life is long or your deeds are good, it is better for you." [[Al-Musnad (5/266).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Abu Yunus, that is Sulaym ibn Jubayr, narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "None of you should wish for death, nor pray for it before it comes to him, unless he is confident in his deeds. For when one of you dies, his deeds come to an end, and a believer's life only increases him in good." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (2/350).]]

This applies when the harm is specific to the person himself. But if it is a trial in the religion, then it is permissible to ask for death, as Allah the Exalted said, reporting about the magicians when Pharaoh wanted to turn them from their religion and threatened them with killing: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims﴾ [al-A'raf: 126]. And Maryam, when the labour pains came upon her, at the trunk of the palm tree, which is the pangs of childbirth, said: ﴿Would that I had died before this and had been a thing forgotten and out of sight﴾ [Maryam: 23], because she knew that people would accuse her of immorality, since she had no husband and yet had conceived and given birth. So someone would say: "How can she have this?" For this reason they confronted her first by saying: ﴿O Maryam, you have certainly come with a monstrous thing. O sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾ [Maryam: 27-28]. Then Allah made for her a way out and a release from that situation, and He caused the infant in the cradle to speak, declaring that he was the servant of Allah and His Messenger. This was a great sign and a dazzling miracle, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

In the hadith of Mu'adh, which Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi narrated, concerning the dream and the supplication contained in it: "When You intend a trial for a people, then take me to You without being subjected to trial." [[Al-Musnad (5/243) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3235. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith. I asked Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari about this hadith, and he said: 'This is a hasan sahih hadith.'"]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Salamah narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad informed us, from Amr, from Asim, from Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Two things the son of Adam dislikes: death, while death is better for the believer than trial; and he dislikes scarcity of wealth, while scarcity of wealth means less reckoning." [[Al-Musnad (5/427).]]

So when trials in the religion arise, it is permissible to ask for death. For this reason Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said at the end of his rule, when he saw that affairs were not coming together for him and that the matter only grew more severe: "O Allah, take me to You, for I have grown weary of them and they have grown weary of me."

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, when those trials befell him and what happened to him with the governor of Khurasan occurred, said: "O Allah, cause me to die and take me to You."

In a hadith: "A man will pass by a grave, that is, in the time of the Dajjal, and he will say: 'Would that I were in its place!'" [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 157/54, from Abu Hurayrah, with the wording: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, the world will not end until a man passes by a grave and rolls himself upon it and says: 'Would that I were in the place of the occupant of this grave,' and there will be no religion left except affliction."]] because of the trials, earthquakes, calamities and terrifying matters that he sees, which are a trial for everyone who is tried.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: It has been mentioned that the sons of Ya'qub, who did to Yusuf what they did, were forgiven by their father, so Allah accepted their repentance, pardoned them, and forgave their sins.

[Mention of the one who said this:]

Al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Hasan narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Salih al-Murri, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When Allah, the Exalted, gathered Ya'qub's family together and comforted him, his sons withdrew for private conversation. Some of them said to others: "Do you not know what you did, and what the Shaykh suffered from you, and what Yusuf suffered from you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Will their pardon of you deceive you? How will you face your Lord?" So their matter settled on coming to the Shaykh, and they sat before him, while Yusuf was sitting beside his father. They said: "O our father, we have come to you about a matter for which we have never come to you before, and a calamity has befallen us the like of which has never befallen us." They kept moving him until he was stirred, and the prophets, peace be upon them, are the most merciful of creation. He said: "What is wrong with you, my sons?" They said: "Do you not know what we did to you, and what we did to our brother Yusuf?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Have you not both pardoned us?" They said: "Yes." They said: "Then your pardon does not avail us anything, if Allah has not pardoned us." He said: "Then what do you want, my sons?" They said: "We want you to pray to Allah for us. When the revelation comes to you from Allah that He has pardoned what we did, our eyes will be comforted and our hearts will be at rest; otherwise, there will never be any comfort of the eye for us in this world." He said: The Shaykh stood up, faced the qiblah, and Yusuf stood behind his father, and they stood behind the two of them, humbled and submissive. He said: He prayed, and Yusuf said "Amin," but He did not answer them for twenty years. (Salih al-Murri said: He kept them in fear.) He said: Until, at the end of the twenty years, Jibril, peace be upon him, descended upon Ya'qub and said: "Allah has sent me to you to give you good news that He has answered your supplication concerning your children, that He has pardoned what they did, and that He has confirmed their covenant with the prophethood after you." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (16/281).]]

This report is a mawquf report from Anas [i.e., it ends with a Companion]. Yazid al-Raqashi and Salih al-Murri are both very weak.

Al-Suddi mentioned that when death came to Ya'qub, peace be upon him, he bequeathed to Yusuf that he should be buried beside Ibrahim and Ishaq. When he died, Yusuf provided for his burial and sent him to al-Sham (Greater Syria), and he was buried beside them, peace be upon them both. [[In manuscripts T and A: "upon them both" instead of "upon them all."]]

Allah says to His servant and messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, after He had related to him the story of Joseph's brothers, and how Allah elevated him over them, granted him the final outcome, victory, kingship and rule, despite what they intended for him of evil, destruction and execution: "This and its like, O Muhammad, is among the reports of the unseen past, ﴿We reveal it to you﴾ and inform you of it, because of the lesson in it for you and the admonition for those who oppose you, ﴿and you were not with them﴾, present among them or witnessing them, ﴿when they agreed upon their plan﴾, that is, to throw him into the well, ﴿while they were scheming﴾ against him. Rather, We informed you of it by revelation sent down to you, as He said: ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens [to see] which of them would be responsible for Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 44]. He also said: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We conveyed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses﴾ [al-Qasas: 44], up to His saying: ﴿Nor were you on the side of the mount when We called, but it is a mercy from your Lord﴾ [al-Qasas: 46].
