Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 12, verses 105–107 (part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, informs of the heedlessness of most people regarding reflection upon the signs of Allah and the proofs of His oneness, [such as] what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth: shining fixed stars and wandering planets and revolving orbits, all of them subjugated; and how many plots of land, adjoining one another, gardens, orchards, firmly rooted mountains, surging seas, tumultuous waves, vast deserts; and how many living and dead beings, animals and plants, and fruits similar and different in taste, scent, color and attributes. Glory be to the One, the Unique, Creator of all kinds of created things, the One alone in everlasting existence, subsistence, and self-sufficiency, possessor of the names and attributes.

And His saying: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: [This refers to] their belief: when they are asked, "Who created the heavens? Who created the earth? Who created the mountains?" they say, "Allah," yet they associate others with Him. Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Thus it is also in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn) that the polytheists used to say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, with no partner for You, except a partner who is Yours; You own him and what he owns." And in the Sahih: that when they said, "Here I am, with no partner for You," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say, "Qad, qad" (enough, enough), meaning: stop, do not add beyond this.

Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is great injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13]. This is the greatest shirk, worshipping another alongside Allah, as in the two Sahihs. From Ibn Mas'ud: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you set up rivals to Allah while He created you."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding His saying: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him﴾: "That is the hypocrite who acts, when he acts, to be seen by people, and he is a polytheist by that deed," referring to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little﴾ [An-Nisa': 142].

There is another, hidden shirk, of which its doer is generally unaware, as narrated by Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from 'Urwah, who said: Hudhayfah entered upon a sick man and saw on his upper arm a thread, so he cut it off, or pulled it away, then recited: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾

And in a hadith: "Whoever swears by other than Allah has associated [others with Allah]." Related by al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan, from the narration of Ibn 'Umar.

And in the hadith related by Ahmad, Abu Dawud and others, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed incantations (ruqa), amulets (tama'im), and love-charms (tiwalah) are shirk."

And in a wording of both of them: "Omens (tiyarah) are shirk, and none of us is free from it, but Allah removes it through reliance (tawakkul)."

Imam Ahmad related it in more detail, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, al-A'mash related to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Yahya al-Jazzar, from the nephew of Zaynab, the wife of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from Zaynab, who said: When 'Abd Allah came from some need and reached the door, he would clear his throat and spit, out of dislike that we should rush upon something he disliked. She said: One day he came, cleared his throat, while with me there was an old woman reciting incantations for me against redness (of the eye), so I put her under the bed. She said: He entered and sat beside me, and saw a thread on my neck. He said, "What is this thread?" I said, "A thread for which I was incanted." She said: He took it and cut it off, then said: "Indeed the family of 'Abd Allah are too well-off for shirk. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Indeed incantations, amulets, and love-charms are shirk.'" She said: I said to him, "Why do you say this? My eye was dripping, and I used to visit so-and-so, the Jew, who would incant it, and when he incanted it, it would calm down." He said: "That was only from the Shaytan. He would prod it with his hand, and when you incant, he withdraws from it. It would suffice you to say what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Remove the harm, Lord of mankind, heal, for You are the Healer; there is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no ailment.'" Related by al-Musnad (1/381).

And in another hadith related by Imam Ahmad, from Waki', from Ibn Abi Layla, from 'Isa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: We entered upon 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ukaym while he was ill, and we were visiting him. It was said to him: "Have you hung something (ta'allaqta shay'an)?" He said: "Shall I hang something, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has said: 'Whoever hangs something is left to it'?" Also related by al-Nasa'i from Abu Hurayrah.

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever hangs an amulet has associated [others with Allah]." And in another narration: "Whoever hangs an amulet, may Allah not complete [his affairs] for him; and whoever hangs a wada'ah (shell), may Allah not leave him in peace." Al-Musnad (4/156); al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib (4/307): "Its narrators are trustworthy."

And from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah says: 'I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of no partner. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his shirk.'" Related by Muslim.

And from Abu Sa'id ibn Abi Fudalah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "When Allah gathers the first and the last for a Day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: Whoever associated anything with Allah in a deed he did for Allah, let him seek its reward from other than Allah, for Allah is the most self-sufficient of partners in need of no partner." Related by Ahmad.

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus related to us, Layth related to us, from Yazid, that is Ibn al-Had, from 'Amr, from Mahmud ibn Labid, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The thing I fear most for you is minor shirk." They said: "And what is minor shirk, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Showing off (riya'). Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection when He recompenses people for their deeds: 'Go to those for whom you used to show off in the world, and see whether you find any reward with them.'" Al-Musnad (5/428); Ibn Hajar graded it hasan in Bulugh al-Maram.

Isma'il ibn Ja'far related it too, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, mawla of al-Muttalib, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, Ibn Hubayrah informed us, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is turned back from a need by an omen has associated [others with Allah]." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the expiation for that?" He said: "That one of them says: 'O Allah, there is no good but Your good, no omen but Your omen, and there is no god besides You.'" Al-Musnad (2/220); Ibn al-Sunni related it in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah (p. 293) through Ibn Wahb from Ibn Lahi'ah, so the hadith is confirmed, praise be to Allah.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr related to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman al-'Arzami related to us, from Abu 'Ali, a man from Banu Kahil, who said: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari addressed us and said: "O people, beware of this shirk, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant." 'Abd Allah ibn Hazn and Qays ibn al-Mudarib stood up and said: "By Allah, you will either retract what you said, or we will go to 'Umar, whether permitted or not." He said: "Rather, I will retract what I said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once addressed us and said: 'O people, beware of this shirk, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant.'" Someone whom Allah willed to ask said: "How can we guard against it, when it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, we seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and we seek Your forgiveness for what we do not know.'" Al-Musnad (4/403).

It has also been narrated by another route, in which the questioner was al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr). Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili related it from the hadith of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Abu Muhammad, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: I witnessed the Prophet ﷺ — or: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq related to me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Shirk is more hidden among you than the crawling of an ant." Abu Bakr said: "Is shirk anything other than one who calls upon another god alongside Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shirk among you is more hidden than the crawling of an ant." Then he said: "Shall I direct you to what removes from you its minor and its major?" Say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know." Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/62). Ibn Jurayj related it from Layth, from Abu Muhammad, from Hudhayfah, similarly; Abu Ya'la also related it in al-Musnad (1/60). Abu Muhammad is unknown (majhul), and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi also related it, from Shaybан ibn Farrukh, from Yahya ibn Kathir, from al-Thawri, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shirk is more hidden in my nation than the crawling of an ant on a smooth rock." He said: Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, then how is salvation and the way out from it?" He said: "Shall I tell you of something which, if you say it, you will be free of its little and its great, its minor and its major?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.'" Related also by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (7/112) through Yahya ibn Muhammad al-Bukhtari, from Shaybān ibn Farrukh, similarly, and he said: "Yahya ibn Kathir alone narrated it from al-Thawri."

Al-Daraqutni said: This Yahya ibn Kathir is called "Abu al-Nadr," and he is matruk al-hadith (abandoned in narration).

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sahih, and al-Nasa'i related from the hadith of Ya'la ibn 'Ata': I heard 'Amr ibn 'Asim [i.e., 'Amr ibn 'Asim] say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me something to say when I rise in the morning, when I reach evening, and when I lie down." He said: "Say: 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself, from the evil of the Shaytan and his shirk.'" Al-Musnad (1/9); Sunan Abi Dawud (5067); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (3392); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7691).

Ahmad added in another narration from the hadith of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, [from Mujahid], from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to say... and he mentioned this supplication and added at its end: "And that I commit against myself an evil or bring it upon a Muslim." Al-Musnad (1/14).

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 12, verses 105–107 (part 2 of 2):

And His saying: ﴿Do they feel secure that an overwhelming punishment from Allah will not come upon them, or the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?﴾ That is: Do these polytheists [in Allah] [[addition from manuscripts T and A]] feel secure that there will not come to them a matter that overwhelms them from where they do not perceive, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive? Or that He will not seize them in their going back and forth, so they cannot escape? Or that He will not seize them with gradual wasting? Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nahl: 45–47] And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping? Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are at play? Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 97–99].

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr related to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman al-'Arzami related to us, from Abu 'Ali, a man from Banu Kahil, who said: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari addressed us and said: "O people, beware of this shirk, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant." 'Abd Allah ibn Hazn and Qays ibn al-Mudarib stood up and said: "By Allah, you will either retract what you said, or we will go to 'Umar, whether permitted or not." He said: "Rather, I will retract what I said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once addressed us and said: 'O people, beware of this shirk, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant.'" Someone whom Allah willed to ask said: "How can we guard against it, when it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, we seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and we seek Your forgiveness for what we do not know.'" Al-Musnad (4/403).

It has also been narrated by another route, in which the questioner was al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr). Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili related it from the hadith of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Abu Muhammad, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: I witnessed the Prophet ﷺ — or: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq related to me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Shirk is more hidden among you than the crawling of an ant." Abu Bakr said: "Is shirk anything other than one who calls upon another god alongside Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shirk among you is more hidden than the crawling of an ant." Then he said: "Shall I direct you to what removes from you its minor and its major?" Say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know." Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/62). Ibn Jurayj related it from Layth, from Abu Muhammad, from Hudhayfah, similarly; Abu Ya'la also related it in al-Musnad (1/60). Abu Muhammad is unknown (majhul), and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi also related it, from Shaybан ibn Farrukh, from Yahya ibn Kathir, from al-Thawri, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shirk is more hidden in my nation than the crawling of an ant on a smooth rock." He said: Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, then how is salvation and the way out from it?" He said: "Shall I tell you of something which, if you say it, you will be free of its little and its great, its minor and its major?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.'" Related also by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (7/112) through Yahya ibn Muhammad al-Bukhtari, from Shaybān ibn Farrukh, similarly, and he said: "Yahya ibn Kathir alone narrated it from al-Thawri."

Al-Daraqutni said: This Yahya ibn Kathir is called "Abu al-Nadr," and he is matruk al-hadith (abandoned in narration).

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sahih, and al-Nasa'i related from the hadith of Ya'la ibn 'Ata': I heard 'Amr ibn 'Asim [i.e., 'Amr ibn 'Asim] say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me something to say when I rise in the morning, when I reach evening, and when I lie down." He said: "Say: 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself, from the evil of the Shaytan and his shirk.'" Al-Musnad (1/9); Sunan Abi Dawud (5067); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (3392); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7691).

Ahmad added in another narration from the hadith of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, [from Mujahid], from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to say... and he mentioned this supplication and added at its end: "And that I commit against myself an evil or bring it upon a Muslim." Al-Musnad (1/14).

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 12, verses 105–107 (part 2 of 2):

And His saying: ﴿Do they feel secure that an overwhelming punishment from Allah will not come upon them, or the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?﴾ That is: Do these polytheists [in Allah] [[addition from manuscripts T and A]] feel secure that there will not come to them a matter that overwhelms them from where they do not perceive, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive? Or that He will not seize them in their going back and forth, so they cannot escape? Or that He will not seize them with gradual wasting? Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nahl: 45–47] And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping? Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are at play? Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 97–99].

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 12, verses 105–107 (part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, informs of the heedlessness of most people regarding reflection upon the signs of Allah and the proofs of His oneness, [such as] what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth: shining fixed stars and wandering planets and revolving orbits, all of them subjugated; and how many plots of land, adjoining one another, gardens, orchards, firmly rooted mountains, surging seas, tumultuous waves, vast deserts; and how many living and dead beings, animals and plants, and fruits similar and different in taste, scent, color and attributes. Glory be to the One, the Unique, Creator of all kinds of created things, the One alone in everlasting existence, subsistence, and self-sufficiency, possessor of the names and attributes.

And His saying: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: [This refers to] their belief: when they are asked, "Who created the heavens? Who created the earth? Who created the mountains?" they say, "Allah," yet they associate others with Him. Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Thus it is also in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn) that the polytheists used to say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, with no partner for You, except a partner who is Yours; You own him and what he owns." And in the Sahih: that when they said, "Here I am, with no partner for You," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say, "Qad, qad" (enough, enough), meaning: stop, do not add beyond this.

Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is great injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13]. This is the greatest shirk, worshipping another alongside Allah, as in the two Sahihs. From Ibn Mas'ud: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you set up rivals to Allah while He created you."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding His saying: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him﴾: "That is the hypocrite who acts, when he acts, to be seen by people, and he is a polytheist by that deed," referring to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little﴾ [An-Nisa': 142].

There is another, hidden shirk, of which its doer is generally unaware, as narrated by Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from 'Urwah, who said: Hudhayfah entered upon a sick man and saw on his upper arm a thread, so he cut it off, or pulled it away, then recited: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾

And in a hadith: "Whoever swears by other than Allah has associated [others with Allah]." Related by al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan, from the narration of Ibn 'Umar.

And in the hadith related by Ahmad, Abu Dawud and others, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed incantations (ruqa), amulets (tama'im), and love-charms (tiwalah) are shirk."

And in a wording of both of them: "Omens (tiyarah) are shirk, and none of us is free from it, but Allah removes it through reliance (tawakkul)."

Imam Ahmad related it in more detail, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, al-A'mash related to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Yahya al-Jazzar, from the nephew of Zaynab, the wife of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from Zaynab, who said: When 'Abd Allah came from some need and reached the door, he would clear his throat and spit, out of dislike that we should rush upon something he disliked. She said: One day he came, cleared his throat, while with me there was an old woman reciting incantations for me against redness (of the eye), so I put her under the bed. She said: He entered and sat beside me, and saw a thread on my neck. He said, "What is this thread?" I said, "A thread for which I was incanted." She said: He took it and cut it off, then said: "Indeed the family of 'Abd Allah are too well-off for shirk. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Indeed incantations, amulets, and love-charms are shirk.'" She said: I said to him, "Why do you say this? My eye was dripping, and I used to visit so-and-so, the Jew, who would incant it, and when he incanted it, it would calm down." He said: "That was only from the Shaytan. He would prod it with his hand, and when you incant, he withdraws from it. It would suffice you to say what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Remove the harm, Lord of mankind, heal, for You are the Healer; there is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no ailment.'" Related by al-Musnad (1/381).

And in another hadith related by Imam Ahmad, from Waki', from Ibn Abi Layla, from 'Isa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: We entered upon 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ukaym while he was ill, and we were visiting him. It was said to him: "Have you hung something (ta'allaqta shay'an)?" He said: "Shall I hang something, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has said: 'Whoever hangs something is left to it'?" Also related by al-Nasa'i from Abu Hurayrah.

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever hangs an amulet has associated [others with Allah]." And in another narration: "Whoever hangs an amulet, may Allah not complete [his affairs] for him; and whoever hangs a wada'ah (shell), may Allah not leave him in peace." Al-Musnad (4/156); al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib (4/307): "Its narrators are trustworthy."

And from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah says: 'I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of no partner. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his shirk.'" Related by Muslim.

And from Abu Sa'id ibn Abi Fudalah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "When Allah gathers the first and the last for a Day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: Whoever associated anything with Allah in a deed he did for Allah, let him seek its reward from other than Allah, for Allah is the most self-sufficient of partners in need of no partner." Related by Ahmad.

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus related to us, Layth related to us, from Yazid, that is Ibn al-Had, from 'Amr, from Mahmud ibn Labid, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The thing I fear most for you is minor shirk." They said: "And what is minor shirk, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Showing off (riya'). Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection when He recompenses people for their deeds: 'Go to those for whom you used to show off in the world, and see whether you find any reward with them.'" Al-Musnad (5/428); Ibn Hajar graded it hasan in Bulugh al-Maram.

Isma'il ibn Ja'far related it too, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, mawla of al-Muttalib, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, Ibn Hubayrah informed us, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is turned back from a need by an omen has associated [others with Allah]." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the expiation for that?" He said: "That one of them says: 'O Allah, there is no good but Your good, no omen but Your omen, and there is no god besides You.'" Al-Musnad (2/220); Ibn al-Sunni related it in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah (p. 293) through Ibn Wahb from Ibn Lahi'ah, so the hadith is confirmed, praise be to Allah.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr related to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman al-'Arzami related to us, from Abu 'Ali, a man from Banu Kahil, who said: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari addressed us and said: "O people, beware of this shirk, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant." He said: "Rather, I will retract what I said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once addressed us and said: 'O people, beware of this shirk, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant.'" Someone whom Allah willed to ask said: "How can we guard against it, when it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, we seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and we seek Your forgiveness for what we do not know.'" Al-Musnad (4/403).

Abu Bakr said: "Is shirk anything other than one who calls upon another god alongside Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shirk among you is more hidden than the crawling of an ant." Then he said: "Shall I direct you to what removes from you its minor and its major?" Say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know." Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/62). Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 12, verses 105–107 (part 2 of 2):

And His saying: ﴿Do they feel secure that an overwhelming punishment from Allah will not come upon them, or the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?﴾ That is: Do these polytheists [in Allah] [[addition from manuscripts T and A]] feel secure that there will not come to them a matter that overwhelms them from where they do not perceive, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive? Or that He will not seize them in their going back and forth, so they cannot escape? Or that He will not seize them with gradual wasting? Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nahl: 45–47] And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping? Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are at play? Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 97–99].

Allah [[added from manuscript A.]] says, addressing His servant and Messenger to the two worlds of mankind and jinn (ath-Thaqalayn: humankind and jinn), commanding him to tell the people: "This is my way (sabil)," that is, his path, his course, and his sunnah. It is the call to the testimony that there is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner. He calls to Allah through it with insight (basirah) into that, with certainty and proof. He and everyone who follows him call to what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called to, with insight, certainty, and both legal (shar'i) and rational proof.

* *

His saying: ﴿And glory be to Allah﴾ means: I declare Allah far above, I exalt Him, magnify Him, and sanctify Him, above having any partner, equal, peer, or rival, or any son, father, or consort, or minister or adviser. He is blessed and exalted, sanctified and far removed from all of that, with a great exaltation. ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing but glorifies His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ [Al-Isra: 44].

He (Allah) informs that He sent His messengers only from among men, not from among women. This is the view of the majority of scholars, as the context of this noble verse indicates: that Allah, exalted is He, did not reveal to any woman among the daughters of Adam a revelation of legislation (wahy tashri', revelation that establishes law).

Some people claimed that Sarah, the wife of the Friend (Abraham), Umm Musa (the mother of Moses), and Maryam (Mary), the mother of 'Isa (Jesus), were prophets. They argued from the fact that the angels gave Sarah the good news of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob; from His saying: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Musa: Suckle him...﴾ [al-Qasas: 7]; and from the fact that the angel came to Maryam and gave her the good news of 'Isa, peace be upon him; and from the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And when the angels said: O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds. O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 42, 43].

This degree of honor is indeed attained by them, but it does not follow from this that they are prophetesses by virtue of it. If the one who claims their prophethood means only this degree of honor, then there is no doubt about it. The discussion then remains with him on whether this, by itself alone, suffices for inclusion in the line of prophethood or not. The position of the Imams of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community), which Shaykh Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Isma'il al-Ash'ari transmitted from them, is that there is no prophetess among women, but among them there are truthful women (siddiqat). As Allah, exalted is He, said, informing about the most noble of them, Maryam bint 'Imran, when He said: ﴿The Messiah, son of Maryam, was not but a messenger; (other) messengers had passed on before him; and his mother was a supremely truthful woman. They both used to eat food﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 75]. So He described her, in her most noble station, as a siddiqah (truthful woman). Had she been a prophetess, He would have mentioned that in the station of honor and exaltation. Thus she is a siddiqah by the explicit text of the Qur'an.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [meaning]: they are not from the people of the heavens, as you say. This statement of Ibn 'Abbas is reinforced by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], and His saying: ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal. Then We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors﴾ [al-Anbiya': 8, 9], and His saying: ﴿Say: I am not something new among the messengers﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿from the people of the towns﴾, what is meant by "towns" (al-qura) is the cities, not that they are from the people of the deserts, who are the most harsh of people in temperament and character. This is the well-known and familiar matter: that the people of cities are gentler in temperament and more refined than the people of their countryside, and the people of the villages and farmland are closer in condition to the people who live in the deserts. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah: 97].

Qatadah said regarding His saying: ﴿from the people of the towns﴾: because they are more knowledgeable and more forbearing than the people of the 'amud (the tent-pole dwellers, i.e., the Bedouins).

In another hadith: a man from the Bedouins gave a she-camel as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he kept giving him gifts and increasing them until he was pleased. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I had resolved not to accept a gift except from a Qurashi, or an Ansari, or a Thaqafi, or a Dawsi." [Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/295) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.]

Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Yahya ibn Wassab, from a shaykh of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, - al-A'mash said: he is [Ibn] 'Umar - from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The believer who mixes with people and bears patiently their harm is better than the one who does not mix with them and does not bear patiently their harm." [al-Musnad (2/43).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth﴾ [meaning: these deniers of you, O Muhammad, in the earth,] ﴿and seen how was the end of those before them﴾, i.e., of the nations that denied the messengers, how Allah destroyed them, and there are similar examples for the disbelievers. Like His saying: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and so have hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. So when they hear the report of that, they will see that Allah destroyed the disbelievers and saved the believers, and this was His sunnah (established way) among His creation. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the Hereafter's home is better for those who fear Allah﴾, i.e., just as We saved the believers in this world, so too We have decreed for them salvation in the Hereafter, and it is far better for them than this world, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand, the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the worst abode﴾ [Ghafir: 50, 51].

He attributed the home to the Hereafter, saying: ﴿and the home of the Hereafter﴾, as it is said: "the prayer of the first" (ṣalat al-ula), "the mosque of the congregation" (masjid al-jami'), "the year of the first" ('am al-awwal), "the night of the first" (barihat al-ula), and "the day of Thursday" (yawm al-khamis). The poet said:

You praise Fa'as and disparage 'Abs,
By Allah, your mother is a mixed-breed (hajin)!

Were the abodes of 'Abs to become desolate for you,
You would know humiliation with the knowledge of certainty.

[The two verses are in Tafsir al-Tabari (16/295).]

He, exalted is He, informs that His help descends upon His messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all, at a time of hardship and while they await relief from Allah, the Exalted, at the moment when they most need it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When will the help of Allah come?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. And in His saying: ﴿...they were denied﴾ there are two readings (qira'at). One of them is with the shadda (emphasis): "qad kuththibu" (they had indeed been denied). Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, used to recite it this way. Al-Bukhari said:

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Salih narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, from Aisha, who said to him, while he was asking her about the saying of Allah: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾: I said: "Akudhibu aw kudhdhibu?" (Were they denied, or were they made to be denied?) Aisha said: "They were made to be denied." I said: "Then they were certain that their people had denied them, so is it not a matter of supposition?" She said: "Indeed, by my life, they were certain of that." I said to her: "And did they think that they had been denied?" She said: "Allah forbid! The messengers would never think that about their Lord." I said: "Then what is this verse?" She said: "They are the followers of the messengers who believed in their Lord and affirmed them, and the trial lasted long for them and the help was delayed from them, ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾ of those among their people who denied them, and the messengers thought that their followers had denied them, then the help of Allah came to them at that time."

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri who said: Urwah informed us. I said: "Perhaps it is 'qad kudhibu' (without the shadda)?" She said: "Allah forbid." End of what he mentioned. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4695, 4696.]

Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me that Ibn Abbas recited it: ﴿And they thought that they had been denied﴾ without the shadda. Abd Allah, who is Ibn Mulaykah, said: Then Ibn Abbas said to me: "They were human beings (bashar)," and Ibn Abbas recited: ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When will the help of Allah come?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah also said to me: Urwah informed me, from Aisha, that she disagreed with that and refused it, and said: "Allah promised Muhammad ﷺ nothing except that he knew it would happen, until he died. But the trial continued upon the messengers until they thought that those among the believers who were with them had denied them." Ibn Abi Mulaykah said in the narration of Urwah: Aisha used to recite it "wa zannu annahum qad kudhdhibu" with the shadda, meaning "they were made to be denied."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us by reading, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who said: A man came to al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and said: "Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi recites this verse: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought they had been denied﴾." Al-Qasim said: "Tell him from me that I heard Aisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, recite: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought they had been denied﴾, and she said: 'Their followers denied them.'" An isnad that is also sahih.

The second reading is with the lighter pronunciation (takhfif), and they differed in its interpretation. Ibn Abbas said what has preceded. Also from Ibn Mas'ud, as narrated by Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abd Allah, that he recited: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾ with lightness (takhfif). Abd Allah said: "It is the one you dislike." [In one manuscript: "it is what he dislikes."]

This narration from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, contradicts what others narrated from them. As for Ibn Abbas, al-A'mash narrated, from Muslim, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾, that he said: "When the messengers despaired that their people would respond to them, and their people thought that the messengers had denied them, the help came to them at that point, ﴿so whom We willed was saved﴾."

The same was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Imran ibn al-Harith al-Sulami, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mu'awiyah, Ali ibn Abi Talhah, and al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas, with the same meaning.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Aarim Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, Shu'ayb narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Abi Hurrah al-Jazari narrated to us, who said: A young man from Quraysh asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr and said to him: "O Abu Abd Allah, how is this letter? When I come to it, I wish I did not recite this surah: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾?" He said: "Yes: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of their people affirming them, and the one sent to them thought that the messengers had lied.'" Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: "I have never seen a man today who is called to knowledge and hesitates! If I had travelled to Yemen for this, it would have been little."

Then Ibn Jarir also narrated from another route: that Muslim ibn Yasar asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about that, and he answered him with this answer. So he got up towards Sa'id, embraced him, and said: "May Allah relieve you of your distress as you relieved me of mine."

Likewise it was narrated from more than one route from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he interpreted it this way. Mujahid ibn Jabr and many of the early scholars (al-salaf) also interpreted it this way. Indeed, Mujahid recited it: "wa zannu annahum qad kadhabu" with a fatha on the dhal. Ibn Jarir narrated it. However, some of those who interpreted it this way refer the pronoun in His saying: ﴿and they thought that they had been denied﴾ to the followers of the messengers among the believers, and some refer it to the disbelievers among them, meaning: "the disbelievers thought that the messengers had lied (kadhabu) – with lightness – concerning what they had been promised of help."

As for Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Jahsh [in some manuscripts: Muhsin] ibn Ziyad al-Dabbi, from Tamim ibn Hadhlam, who said: "I heard Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud say concerning this verse: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾ of their people's faith, that they would believe in them, and their people thought, when the matter was delayed, that they had lied, with lightness."

These two narrations from each of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas differ, and Aisha rejected this interpretation from those who explained it that way. Ibn Jarir defended her, supported the view of the majority, rejected the other view entirely, refuted it and its proponent, and did not accept it or approve of it. And Allah knows best.

[See what Aisha said in Tafsir al-Tabari (16/307, 308) and al-Tabari's refutation of Ibn Abbas's view (16/306).]

Allah the Exalted says: "Certainly in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding (ulu al-albab)." Their stories with their peoples, and how We saved the believers and destroyed the disbelievers. ﴿A lesson for those of understanding﴾, and "al-albab" means the minds (al-uqul). ﴿It is not a narration that could be invented﴾, meaning: this Qur'an could not be fabricated apart from Allah, that is, it could not be denied or fabricated. ﴿But it is a confirmation of what came before it﴾, meaning of the Books sent down from heaven, and it confirms what is correct in them, negates what has occurred in them of distortion, alteration and change, and judges them by abrogation (naskh) or affirmation. ﴿And a detailed explanation of all things﴾ regarding what is lawful and unlawful, what is beloved and disliked, and other matters: the commanding of acts of obedience, obligatory duties and recommended acts, and the forbidding of prohibited acts and what resembles them of disliked acts; the reporting of matters that are evident, and of unseen future events, both general and detailed; and the reporting of the Lord, blessed and exalted, through His names and attributes, and His being declared free from resemblance to created beings. Therefore it is ﴿a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe﴾, by which their hearts are guided from error to right guidance, and from misguidance to rectitude, and by which they seek mercy from the Lord of the servants, in this worldly life and on the Day of Return. So we ask Allah the Mighty that He make us among them in this world and the Hereafter, on the Day when the faces that are radiant and bright will prevail with the gain, and the faces that are blackened will return with the losing bargain.

The end of the commentary on Surah Yusuf. All praise and grace belong to Allah, in Him is help sought and upon Him is reliance, and He is sufficient for us and the best Disposer of affairs.
